The discount depends on what system you are replacing, the size and efficiency of the new unit, and current certificate prices. You must involve a VEU accredited provider (or an installer working with one) before any installation work begins. $630 to $1,610 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 How Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discounts work for homes The Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program provides upfront, point-of-sale discounts when Victorian households replace older heating, cooling, and hot water equipment with approved high-efficiency electric alternatives. Rather than applying for a cash refund after you pay, a VEU accredited provider calculates the Victorian Energy Efficiency Certificates (VEECs) your upgrade creates and deducts that value from your quote. Involve an accredited provider before any work starts Energy Victoria strongly advises contacting a VEU accredited provider (or using an installer who works with one) before you buy or install any equipment. Retrospective discounts after installation work has started are typically not possible. Read our detailed guide on the VEU timing rule . Reverse-cycle air conditioning discounts in Victoria Many headlines quote the largest possible VEU figure ( up to $5,530 [source] ), which applies only when decommissioning a whole-home ducted gas heater and installing a large 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system. For a typical Victorian home replacing a non-ducted room gas heater with a single split system (3 to 9 kW), Energy Victoria lists an indicative discount of $630 to $1,610 [source] . Energy Victoria also estimates annual energy bill savings of up to $460 [source] per year when switching from a room gas heater to a split system, and up to $1,140 [source] per year when replacing ducted gas with ducted reverse-cycle heating. Heat pump and solar-boosted hot water discounts Under the VEU hot water activity, the indicative discount depends on whether your existing water heater runs on electricity or mains gas: Replacing an inefficient electric storage water heater with an approved heat pump has an indicative VEU discount of $630 [source] . Replacing an inefficient gas water heater with an approved heat pump has an indicative VEU discount of $560 [source] . Every VEU hot water upgrade requires a minimum customer co-contribution of $200 [source] , and the building must be at least two years old. Eligible households can also combine the VEU discount with the Solar Victoria Solar Homes hot water rebate for combined savings of up to $1,560 [source] (or up to $1,960 [source] when choosing an eligible locally made product). Switching from gas to efficient electric hot water saves around $400 [source] a year on bills according to Energy Victoria. Victoria’s 1 March 2027 gas hot water replacement rule From 1 March 2027 , when a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing Victorian home reaches the end of its life and needs replacing, it cannot be replaced with another mains gas water heater. It must be replaced with an efficient electric system such as a heat pump or solar-boosted water heater, unless an exemption applies. Bottled LPG systems are not affected, and owner-occupiers are not required to replace existing gas space heating or gas cooktops. For rental properties, new minimum efficiency standards also begin on 1 March 2027 when a hot water unit or main living area heater fails Beyond repair, and for main living area cooling at the start of a new lease. Read our full breakdown in the 1 March 2027 Gas to Electric Hot Water guide . Frequently asked questions Can I claim a Victorian Energy Upgrades discount after my system is already installed? Generally no. Energy Victoria advises that you must contact an accredited provider (or use an installer working with one) before buying or installing your system. Retrospective discounts after installation work has started are typically not possible. See our guide on /victoria/reverse-cycle-vs-gas-heater/ for how the timing rule works. Why does the air conditioner discount vary so much between homes? The Victorian Energy Upgrades discount is calculated from the greenhouse gas savings of your specific upgrade. Replacing a whole-home ducted gas heater with a high-capacity ducted reverse-cycle system creates far more certificates than replacing a single room gas heater or installing a split system without decommissioning an existing heater. Compare the full scenario tables on /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/. Why is the VEU heat pump discount different when replacing gas versus electric hot water? Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades methodology, replacing an inefficient electric resistance water heater saves more calculated emissions than replacing a mains gas water heater, so the point-of-sale discount differs between the two scenarios. Check the exact figures for both replacement types on /victoria/heat-pump-rebate/. What happens on 1 March 2027 when a gas hot water system breaks down? From 1 March 2027, when a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing Victorian home reaches the end of its life and needs replacing, it generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas unit and must be replaced with an electric alternative such as a heat pump or solar-boosted system. Exemptions apply for certain technical constraints, and bottled LPG systems are not affected. Read the full details on /victoria/gas-to-electric-hot-water-2027/. How we are paid Writing and maintaining accurate, source-checked guides takes time. Our business model is straightforward: No cost to households: Reading our guides and using the Victoria Eligibility Checker is free and does not require entering your contact details. Named installer enquiries (when open): When we have a signed written agreement with one to three vetted installers covering your postcode, you can choose to submit a quote request form. Lead fee: Participating installers pay Agenor Services Pty Ltd a flat fee for each valid, consented quote enquiry we pass to them. Strict consent boundaries: We never sell your details to unnamed lead brokers, never pre-tick consent boxes, and always name the exact installer and their VEU accredited provider on the form before you decide whether to submit. While we have no signed installer for an activity or postcode, our form remains closed and points you directly to Energy Victoria’s official directory. Editorial and fact-checking method Many rebate websites confuse electric-to-heat-pump figures with gas-to-heat-pump figures, or advertise the maximum ducted gas replacement discount as if every split system qualifies for it. To prevent that: Every dollar figure on Household Rebates comes from a single structured data file backed by an official government publication. Every figure displays the date we last checked it against the official page and a direct link to that source. An automated build check fails if any figure is more than 45 days old or if an unverified dollar figure appears anywhere in our templates or articles. See our full list of primary documents on the Sources and Method page . Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home How VEU Quotes, Installers and Consumer Rights Work How VEU Quotes, Installers and Consumer Rights Work Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program, upfront discounts are delivered through accredited providers and the licensed installers who work with them. You must contact an accredited provider or participating installer before any work starts so they can verify your existing equipment, confirm your exact point-of-sale discount in writing, and record compliance evidence. Lead generation and marketing are regulated under the VEU code of conduct, which bans cold calling and doorknocking without express prior consent. By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 How to get a Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) quote safely Check your current system and building age before buying anything. Confirm what type of heater or water heater you are replacing and whether your home is more than two years old. Do not remove your existing unit or start installation work yet. Contact a named installer working with a VEU accredited provider. Give express prior consent to be contacted by a specific installation business that works with a named VEU accredited provider, or contact an accredited provider directly from Energy Victoria's directory. Get a written quote showing the accredited provider and exact discount. Before any work starts, review the written quote confirming the approved product model, minimum 5-year household warranty, the accredited provider creating the certificates, the point-of-sale VEU discount, and your co-contribution. Complete pre-installation evidence and licensed installation. Allow the installer to record required pre-installation photos and serial numbers before decommissioning your old unit, and receive your compliance certificates upon completion. Roles: licensed installers vs VEU accredited providers Two parties are typically involved in a household upgrade under the Victorian Energy Upgrades program: The licensed installer (electrician, plumber, or HVAC technician): Measures your home, supplies and installs the approved reverse-cycle air conditioner or heat pump water heater, decommissions the old system, and issues plumbing/electrical compliance certificates. The VEU accredited provider (accredited person): Authorised by the Essential Services Commission (ESC) to create Victorian Energy Efficiency Certificates (VEECs) once the upgrade evidence is verified. Some large installers are accredited providers themselves; many local installers partner with an accredited provider. You must know who the accredited provider is Under the Essential Services Commission’s lead generation and marketing rules ( ESC Lead Generation Fact Sheet v1.2 ), you must be told the name of the accredited person creating the certificates for your upgrade. Your rights under the VEU code of conduct Every accredited provider, installer, and lead generator participating in the Victorian Energy Upgrades program must follow the VEU code of conduct enforced by the Essential Services Commission: Ban on cold calls and doorknocking: Telemarketing cold calls have been banned since 1 May 2024 , and unsolicited doorknocking has been banned since 1 August 2024 , unless you have given express prior consent ( ESC Telemarketing and Doorknocking Bans FAQ v1.1 ). 3-month consent limit: When you give express prior consent via an online enquiry form, that consent lasts for 3 months unless you withdraw it sooner or explicitly agree to a different period. Channel and recipient specificity: You choose whether you consent to be contacted by phone, email, and/or a home visit to measure and quote, and the consent form names the installation partner who will contact you. Accurate, honest information: Marketers and installers must not claim to work for the Victorian Government, the VEU program, or the Essential Services Commission, and must not promise a discount before checking your eligibility. We do not use tracking cookies or third-party advertising pixels on this website. By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Draft pending legal review before quote form activation This Privacy Policy and APP 5 Collection Notice is our complete operational draft ( version: 2026-11-13-v1 ). Our quote request form remains switched off until a qualified Australian privacy and consumer law practitioner reviews and signs off on this wording. 1. Who we are This website ( householdrebates.com.au , Household Rebates ) is operated by Agenor Services Pty Ltd (ABN 29 644 447 263 ), located in Melbourne, Victoria, Australia ( we , us , our ). Under the Privacy Act 1988 (Cth), disclosing personal information to another organisation for a commercial benefit (such as a lead generation fee) is classified as “trading in personal information” ( OAIC — Trading in personal information ). Accordingly, we comply with the Australian Privacy Principles (APPs) and obtain your express consent before passing any enquiry to a participating installer. 2. APP 5 Collection Notice (when you submit a quote form) When our quote enquiry form is active and you choose to submit it: What we collect: Your first name, optional last name, email address, phone number, Victorian postcode, property tenure (owner, renter, or landlord), whether the building is over 2 years old, current heating/hot water system, upgrade interest, preferred contact channels (phone, email, and/or home visit), optional notes, how you heard about us, and the exact wording and timestamp of your consent. What we do not collect: We do not ask for your street address, date of birth, income, concession card numbers, or government identifiers on our form. Why we collect it: To pass your quote enquiry to the named participating installer(s) shown on the form (who work with the named Victorian Energy Upgrades accredited provider) so they can contact you via your selected channel(s) about a quote, and to maintain an auditable record of your express prior consent under the VEU code of conduct. Commercial benefit disclosure: The participating installer pays Agenor Services Pty Ltd a fee for each valid enquiry we send them. If you do not provide this information: We cannot pass a quote enquiry to a participating installer. You can still browse all guides, use the Eligibility Checker anonymously, or contact an accredited provider directly from Energy Victoria’s website. 3. Express prior consent and how to withdraw it (3-month limit) In accordance with the Essential Services Commission’s rules under the VEU code of conduct ( ESC Telemarketing and Doorknocking Bans FAQ v1.1 ): Your express prior consent to be contacted by the named installer lasts for 3 months from the date you submit the form, unless you withdraw it earlier. How to withdraw consent: You can withdraw your consent at any time by replying to your confirmation email or emailing privacy@householdrebates.com.au with your email address or reference number ( HR-XXXXXX ). When you withdraw consent, we record your withdrawal timestamp and notify each installer who received your enquiry to cease contact immediately. 4. Cookies, analytics, and server logs No tracking cookies: We do not set analytics or advertising cookies in your browser, and we do not load third-party tracking scripts. Eligibility Checker: Your answers in the Eligibility Checker stay in your browser ( sessionStorage only if you proceed to the form on the same visit). Server logs and rate limiting: Our web server records standard access logs (kept for 30 days) and a separate AI-referrer log that excludes IP addresses (kept for 180 days). When you submit a form, we store a one-way cryptographic hash ( HMAC-SHA256 ) of your IP address solely to enforce anti-spam rate limits; your raw IP address is never stored in our database. 5. Data storage, security, and retention periods All enquiry and consent records are stored in an access-restricted SQLite database on our Australian-managed server environment with encrypted daily backups ( age encryption). Record category Retention period Action at end of period Personal contact details (name, email, phone, message) 12 months from creation Permanently nulled by our automated nightly purge job ( status = purged ) ip_hash and user_agent on enquiries 30 days from creation Nulled by our automated nightly purge job Consent audit record (version, SHA-256 hash, snapshot, scopes, timestamps) 24 months after expiry or withdrawal Deleted after the VEU audit window closes Delivery and invoicing metadata (installer ID, timestamp, fee) 7 years Retained for Australian taxation compliance (contains no personal contact details after purge) 6. Access, correction, deletion, and complaints You may request access to, correction of, or erasure of your personal information held by us at any time by emailing privacy@householdrebates.com.au . We respond to all privacy requests within 30 days. If you have a complaint about how we have handled your personal information, please contact privacy@householdrebates.com.au first. If you are not satisfied with our response, you may contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner (OAIC) at www.oaic.gov.au or on 1300 363 992 . Which upgrades does Victorian Energy Upgrades cover? Under Energy Victoria’s current household product list ( Energy Victoria — VEU products ), accredited providers offer upfront point-of-sale discounts on approved: Heating and cooling: high-efficiency reverse-cycle split, multi-split, and ducted air conditioners. Hot water systems: air-source heat pump and solar-boosted water heaters replacing inefficient electric or gas systems. Ceiling insulation: under-insulated or uninsulated ceilings (for example, up to $1,500 [source] on an average 150 m² metropolitan Melbourne house). Induction cooktops: built-in or freestanding units replacing an existing gas cooktop. Building envelope and appliances: weather sealing (draught proofing), window glazing, efficient showerheads, clothes dryers, fridges and freezers, in-home displays, and televisions. Every VEU figure on our site is linked to its primary government publication—see our Official Sources and Verification Method page or return to the Household Rebates home page . What changes in Victoria in 2027? Three key Victorian Government rule changes begin in 2027 ( Energy Victoria — Electrification and efficiency standards , Solar Victoria — Solar PV support moving into VEU ): 1 January 2027 — All-electric new homes: New residential buildings requiring a building permit must be built all-electric without reticulated mains gas connections. 1 March 2027 — Existing gas hot water replacements and rental standards: When a mains gas water heater in an existing home fails and needs replacing, it must switch to an efficient electric alternative unless an exemption applies. Phased minimum energy efficiency standards for rental properties also start from 1 March 2027. 1 July 2027 — Solar PV moves into VEU: Residential solar panel support transitions from Solar Homes into the Victorian Energy Upgrades program, with current Solar Homes solar panel rebates continuing until 30 June 2027. To check which current discount scenario matches your home before speaking with an installer, open the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Which home upgrades does the Victorian Energy Upgrades program cover? Energy Victoria lists household VEU discounts across heating and cooling, hot water systems, induction cooktops, ceiling insulation, clothes dryers, window glazing, weather sealing, efficient showerheads, fridges and freezers, in-home displays, and televisions. Each product category has its own eligibility rules and approved product register. What changes for Victorian homes in 2027? Three major dates take effect in 2027: new residential buildings must be built all-electric from 1 January 2027, existing mains gas water heaters that fail and need replacement must switch to efficient electric alternatives from 1 March 2027 unless exempt, and phased minimum energy efficiency standards for rental properties start from 1 March 2027. What happens to Solar Victoria solar panel rebates from July 2027? Solar Victoria has announced that residential solar PV support will transition into the Victorian Energy Upgrades program from 1 July 2027, while current Solar Homes solar panel rebate arrangements remain in place until 30 June 2027. A single split system replacing a room gas heater carries a smaller discount than a whole-home ducted gas replacement, and smaller discounts still apply when no old heater is decommissioned. You must engage a VEU accredited provider (or an installer working with one) before buying or installing the unit. $630 to $1,610 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Why the headline figure only applies to the largest ducted systems You will often see marketing advertisements quote up to $5,530 [source] off air conditioning in Victoria. According to Energy Victoria’s heating and cooling discount tables, up to $5,530 [source] is the maximum indicative discount for replacing a whole-home ducted gas heater with a 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system . Smaller homes or single-room upgrades receive different discounts based on the energy savings calculated for that specific scenario: Replacing a non-ducted (room) gas heater with a 3 to 9 kW split system: $630 to $1,610 [source] (see our gas room heater to split-system swap guide ). Replacing a ducted gas heater with a 10 kW, 16 kW, or 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system: up to $2,520 [source] (10 kW) or up to $4,200 [source] (16 kW) (see our ducted gas to ducted reverse-cycle swap guide ). Replacing a ducted gas heater with a multi-split system ( up to $2,940 [source] ) or four single split systems ( up to $2,520 [source] ) (see our ducted gas to split systems guide ). Replacing a hard-wired electric heater or central electric ducted heater with reverse-cycle air conditioning (see our electric heater to reverse-cycle guide ). Installing a new split system without decommissioning an existing heater: $70 to $140 [source] (or up to $410 [source] for a ducted unit without decommissioning). The VEU discount comes off the price in your quote, but you still pay at least this minimum amount yourself—so any advertisement or cold call offering a “free” or near-free ducted air conditioner cannot be a legitimate VEU offer. Read more on how the VEU minimum customer co-payment works . Eligibility requirements for Victorian homes To access a VEU heating and cooling discount, your installation must meet Energy Victoria’s household rules: Approved product: The unit must be a high-efficiency reverse-cycle air conditioner listed on the VEU Register of Products that both heats and cools. Minimum warranty: For household installations, the product must carry a minimum 5-year warranty . Property age: If you are replacing an existing heating system, the property must be more than 2 years old . Accredited provider involvement before work starts: You must work with a VEU accredited provider, or a licensed installer partnered with one, before any installation or decommissioning work starts. Do not decommission your old gas heater first If you remove your old gas heater or install your new air conditioner before a VEU accredited provider has collected the required pre-installation evidence, you will generally lose access to the discount. Read our guide on the VEU timing and decommissioning rules . Estimated annual energy bill savings Alongside the upfront installation discount, Energy Victoria publishes indicative annual running-cost savings for households switching from gas to efficient reverse-cycle heating: Replacing a room gas heater with a split-system air conditioner saves up to $460 [source] per year on energy bills. Replacing a ducted gas heater with a ducted reverse-cycle system saves up to $1,140 [source] per year on energy bills. Rules for renters and landlords Rental properties in Victoria are eligible for VEU heating and cooling discounts. If you are a renter, you must obtain your landlord’s written permission before any heating or cooling work takes place. From 1 March 2027 , Victorian rental minimum standards also require landlords to install an efficient reverse-cycle air conditioner in the main living area when an existing heater breaks down and cannot be repaired, and require efficient cooling in the main living area at the start of a new lease. Frequently asked questions Why does the air conditioner discount vary so much between homes? The Victorian Energy Upgrades discount is calculated from the greenhouse gas savings of your specific upgrade. Replacing a whole-home ducted gas heater with a high-capacity ducted reverse-cycle system creates far more certificates than replacing a single room gas heater or installing a split system without decommissioning an existing heater. Compare the full scenario tables on /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/. Is there a minimum I have to pay for a ducted system? Yes. Under Victorian Energy Upgrades Specifications version 25.0 (Part 6), every household heating and cooling upgrade requires a minimum customer co-payment that took effect on 30 September 2026, so the discount cannot cover the full cost of the system. Check the current co-payment tiers by system type in the minimum customer co-payment section at /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/#the-minimum-you-pay-from-30-september-2026. Can I claim a Victorian Energy Upgrades discount after my system is already installed? Generally no. Energy Victoria advises that you must contact an accredited provider (or use an installer working with one) before buying or installing your system. Retrospective discounts after installation work has started are typically not possible. See our guide on /victoria/reverse-cycle-vs-gas-heater/ for how the timing rule works. Are rental properties eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades discounts? Yes, rental properties in Victoria can access VEU discounts for approved reverse-cycle air conditioners and hot water upgrades, provided the building is more than two years old when replacing an existing system. Renters must have the landlord's approval before any heating, cooling, or hot water installation takes place. From 1 March 2027, new rental minimum efficiency standards also apply when systems fail or at the start of a new lease. Quote requests are not open yet We're not taking quote requests yet. VEU Retrospective Discounts in Victoria Already Installed? VEU Retrospective Discounts in Victoria Retrospective Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discounts after an appliance has already been installed are possible only in very limited circumstances and are never assured. Any retrospective claim must be processed by a willing accredited provider within six months of the end of the calendar year in which the upgrade occurred, backed by full invoices, compliance certificates, decommissioning records, and geo-tagged before-and-after photos. Claims are simpler where no old appliance had to be decommissioned, such as eligible induction cooktops. By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Why retrospective VEU claims are rare Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades program, discounts are designed to be arranged before installation starts ( how VEU quotes work ). Energy Victoria warns that retrospective discounts—claiming after an upgrade is already installed—are available only in very limited cases and are not assured ( Energy Victoria — Retrospective discounts ). Accredited providers are under no obligation to process a retrospective claim, and most cannot create certificates if required pre-installation evidence was missed before the old heater or hot water unit left the property. Strict six-month calendar-year deadline Even if you have every document and find a willing provider ( how to find a VEU accredited provider ), VEU rules set a hard statutory cut-off ( Energy Victoria — Retrospective discounts ): Certificates for a completed upgrade must be processed within 6 months of the end of the calendar year in which the installation took place. For example, an upgrade installed in December 2025 had to be processed by 30 June 2026 ; an upgrade installed anywhere in 2026 must be processed by 30 June 2027 . Evidence you must supply to an accredited provider To assess whether a retrospective claim is even possible, an accredited provider typically needs all of the following ( Energy Victoria — Retrospective discounts ): Itemised tax invoice showing the exact brand and model number of the VEU-approved product installed. Electrical and/or plumbing compliance certificates issued by the licensed tradespeople who performed the work. Decommissioning and disposal evidence proving how the old gas or electric appliance was permanently removed and disposed of. Geo-tagged before-and-after photographs of the old equipment in situ prior to removal and the new equipment installed. Upgrades without decommissioning (including induction cooktops) Energy Victoria notes that retrospective claims are easier where no existing appliance had to be decommissioned ( Energy Victoria — Retrospective discounts ). For induction cooktops , households can buy an approved unit from a retailer and claim the discount afterwards through a participating provider—note that induction cooktops purchased before 30 June 2026 must appear on the older Part 46 product list to qualify ( Energy Victoria — Induction cooktop discounts ). If you have not started your next upgrade yet, check your options first in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions What is the strict deadline for processing a retrospective VEU discount? Energy Victoria states that any retrospective claim must be processed by an accredited provider within six months of the end of the calendar year in which the upgrade took place (for example, a December 2025 upgrade had to be processed by 30 June 2026). What documents and photos are needed for a retrospective VEU claim? Energy Victoria lists itemised tax invoices showing brand and model numbers, electrical or plumbing compliance certificates, decommissioning and disposal evidence, and geo-tagged before-and-after photographs. Does decommissioning an old unit or buying an induction cooktop before 30 June 2026 affect a retrospective claim? Energy Victoria notes that retrospective claims are easier where no existing system had to be decommissioned (since missing pre-removal photos usually block replacement claims), and induction cooktops purchased before 30 June 2026 must appear on the older Part 46 product list. Multi-unit Class 2 buildings on centralised gas hot water are exempt from the 1 March 2027 individual gas water heater replacement rule, and rental minimum standards also exempt properties with centralised systems or no external compressor space. up to $2,800 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Solar Victoria ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 VEU eligibility for individual units and owners corporations Energy Victoria confirms that both individual apartment owners and owners corporations can participate in the Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program ( Energy Victoria — Renters, landlords and body corporate ): Owners corporations: Eligible under VEU residential activities (for Class 1, Class 2, Class 3, or Class 4 buildings) or commercial activities depending on the building’s classification and common-property plant. Individual apartments and units: Can claim VEU discounts on lot-specific upgrades—for example, Energy Victoria’s weather sealing page lists apartment draught-proofing discounts of $70 [source] (with a 2-year warranty) or $140 [source] (with a 5-year warranty) ( Energy Victoria — Weather sealing discounts ). Check your owners-corporation rules before installing any external split-system or heat pump unit on common property or balconies. Centralised gas hot water and 2027 rules Apartment buildings face distinct technical rules under Victoria’s 2027 standards: 1 March 2027 gas hot water rule: Regulation 45E(3) explicitly exempts a Class 2 building (such as an apartment block) served by a centralised gas hot water system ( Building and Plumbing Amendment Regulations 2025 — reg 45E text ; see all regulation 45E exemptions ). 2027 rental minimum standards: Consumer Affairs Victoria includes exemptions where a rented apartment is served by centralised heating, cooling, or hot water, lacks space for an outdoor compressor, or is restricted by owners-corporation rules ( Consumer Affairs Victoria — Minimum energy efficiency standards ; see Victorian landlord 2027 standards ). Solar for Apartments program (Solar Victoria) Separate from the standalone-home Solar Homes solar PV rebate ( compare VEU vs Solar Homes ), Solar Victoria runs Solar for Apartments to help owners corporations install shared rooftop solar PV across multi-unit residential buildings ( Solar Victoria — Solar for Apartments ): Solar for Apartments funding: Solar for Apartments provides up to $2,800 [source] per participating apartment and up to $140,000 [source] per apartment property, open until 30 June 2027 or until funding is exhausted. Program expansion: Solar Victoria is expanding the program—including removing the median property value limit ( Solar Victoria — Expanding solar savings to more Victorians ). Check the current eligibility rules on its page before your owners corporation applies, and test individual lot upgrades in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Can apartment owners and owners corporations access VEU discounts? Yes. Energy Victoria confirms that owners corporations are eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades either under residential activities (for Class 1, 2, 3, or 4 buildings) or commercial activities depending on building classification, and individual lot owners can also upgrade lot-specific appliances where owners-corporation rules allow. How does Victoria’s 2027 gas hot water rule apply to apartments on centralised gas? Regulation 45E(3) exempts Class 2 apartment buildings served by a centralised gas hot water system from the 1 March 2027 mains gas water heater replacement restriction. Rental minimum standards also include exemptions where centralised systems, lack of external compressor space, or owners-corporation rules prevent an individual electric installation; see /victoria/gas-hot-water-ban-exemptions/. How does Solar Victoria’s Solar for Apartments program work? Solar Victoria’s Solar for Apartments program helps owners corporations install shared solar PV across multi-unit residential buildings, running until 30 June 2027 or until funding is exhausted. Because Solar Victoria announced a program expansion removing the median property value cap and raising the lot threshold while updating its main program page, check Solar Victoria’s Solar for Apartments page directly for current lot rules. Can You Claim VEU Twice or Stack Other Rebates in Victoria? Whether you can claim a Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discount more than once depends on the product activity—households can upgrade up to two hot water systems, while the induction cooktop discount requires that you have not previously claimed one. You can also claim across separate upgrade categories and stack a VEU hot water discount with federal Small-scale Technology Certificates (STCs) and the Solar Homes hot water rebate on the same eligible installation. For heating and cooling repeat-claim rules at your address, ask the accredited provider before work starts. up to $1,560 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Repeat limits by VEU upgrade activity Claiming a VEU discount on one appliance does not lock your home out of the rest of the Victorian Energy Upgrades program—for example, a household that upgraded hot water can still look into heating and cooling, ceiling insulation, or an induction cooktop. Within each activity, official Energy Victoria guidance sets out the following rules: Hot water systems: Victorian households can upgrade up to 2 hot water systems under VEU (while businesses can upgrade up to 5) ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ). See gas hot water to heat pump discounts for household scenarios. Induction cooktops: To be eligible, you must not have previously claimed a VEU induction cooktop discount ( Energy Victoria — Induction cooktop discounts ). Read more in our gas cooktop to induction guide . Heating and cooling: Energy Victoria’s consumer heating and cooling page does not state a single household unit cap across every scenario— ask the accredited provider to check previous VEU certificate creations at your address and confirm how many systems qualify before any work begins. Stacking VEU, Solar Homes, and STCs on hot water On an eligible heat pump or solar hot water upgrade, three incentives can work together on the same installation ( Solar Victoria — Hot water rebate ; Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ): Federal STCs (Small-scale Technology Certificates): Applied as an upfront point-of-sale discount by your installer. Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discount: Applied upfront by your VEU accredited provider. Solar Homes hot water rebate: Calculated after STCs and VEECs have been deducted, provided you are an eligible owner-occupier, obtain Solar Victoria pre-approval before installation, and your property address has not previously received a Solar Homes hot water rebate or battery rebate. Energy Victoria states that combining the VEU hot water discount with the Solar Homes hot water rebate saves households up to $1,560 [source] , or up to $1,960 [source] when choosing an eligible locally made product. Compare the full eligibility rules in VEU vs Solar Homes and our Heat Pump Hot Water Rebate Victoria guide , or test your setup in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions How many hot water systems can a household upgrade under the VEU program? Energy Victoria states that households can upgrade up to two hot water systems under the Victorian Energy Upgrades program, while businesses can upgrade up to five systems. Can I claim the VEU induction cooktop discount more than once? No. Energy Victoria's induction cooktop eligibility rules state that you must not have previously claimed a VEU induction cooktop discount. Can I claim a Solar Homes hot water rebate if my address already had one? Solar Victoria's hot water rebate rules state that the property address must not have previously received a Solar Homes hot water rebate or a Solar Homes battery rebate, whereas VEU and Federal STCs can still apply if their separate conditions are met. Energy Victoria publishes higher indicative figures for cold regional postcodes than mild metropolitan Melbourne postcodes, and mandatory electrical and installer safety checks apply before any work begins. up to $1,500 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Mandatory electrical and ceiling safety checks come first Before any ceiling insulation can be installed under the Victorian Energy Upgrades program, Energy Victoria requires two separate safety assessments ( Energy Victoria — Ceiling insulation discounts ; Solar Victoria — Ceiling insulation discounts news ): Pre-installation electrical safety assessment by a licensed electrician: Checks roof-space wiring, downlights, exhaust fans, and clearances. Installer safety assessment by an EEC-certified installer: Installers must be certified by the Energy Efficiency Council (EEC) and complete an on-site hazard check before work starts. Halogen downlights and unsafe wiring block eligibility until fixed Energy Victoria states that homes with recessed halogen downlights or unsafe electrical wiring are ineligible for VEU ceiling insulation until those hazards are rectified by a licensed electrician. Never lay insulation over unrated downlights or untested wiring. Indicative VEU discounts: metropolitan vs regional postcodes With Stage 2 open to all eligible Victorian homes, Energy Victoria estimates that almost 60% [source] of Victorian homes have no ceiling insulation or too little, and expects the VEU discount to cut installation cost by about 30 to 50% [source] while saving more than $400 [source] a year on energy bills. Household VEU ceiling insulation examples (150 m² house) · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 against Ceiling insulation discounts — Victorian Energy Upgrades (Energy Victoria (DEECA)) ↗ . Indicative. The accredited provider confirms the final amount in your quote. Upgrade scenario Indicative VEU discount Average 150 m² house, metro Melbourne (mild climate zone) up to $1,500 Average 150 m² house, regional Victoria (cold climate zone) up to $2,100 Why do the two examples ( up to $1,500 [source] vs up to $2,100 [source] ) differ? The VEU Specifications version 25.0 postcode table ( Location Variable List , VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ) sets how each Victorian postcode is classified (such as metropolitan mild versus regional cold postcodes like Ballarat ), and the accredited provider confirms the exact discount in your written quote. Enter your postcode in our Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker to inspect your postcode’s classification right in your browser. Under VEU Specifications version 25.0 (activity 48), a mandatory minimum customer co-payment of at least $200 (including GST) [source] also applies ( see all VEU minimum co-payments ). Is your ceiling eligible (uninsulated or below R2.0)? To qualify under Energy Victoria’s household rules, your ceiling must be either: Completely uninsulated , or Under-insulated below R2.0 —which Energy Victoria describes as existing batts or loose-fill measuring roughly 90 mm thick or sitting lower than a ceiling joist . Combining ceiling insulation with weather sealing (draught proofing) helps stop heated air escaping around doors, vents, and wall gaps. Rental properties and the R5.0 standard from 1 March 2027 Under Victoria’s minimum energy efficiency standards for rental properties ( Energy Victoria — Energy efficiency for rental properties ), rental homes with no ceiling insulation must have at least R5.0 ceiling insulation installed at the start of a new lease from 1 March 2027 , unless an exemption applies ( read our Victorian landlord 2027 guide and our Victorian renters guide ). Frequently asked questions How do I know if my ceiling insulation is low enough to qualify for the VEU discount? Energy Victoria states that a Victorian home is eligible if the ceiling is uninsulated or has existing ceiling insulation rated below R2.0, which is roughly 90 mm thick or sitting lower than the height of a ceiling joist. An accredited provider's certified installer inspects and confirms your ceiling before work starts. Why are Energy Victoria's metro and regional ceiling insulation examples different? Colder regional postcodes achieve higher calculated heating energy savings from ceiling insulation than milder metropolitan Melbourne postcodes, creating more certificates under the VEU formula. The VEU Specifications postcode table sets how each Victorian postcode is classified, and your accredited provider confirms the exact figure. What happens if my ceiling has halogen downlights or unsafe electrical wiring? Under Energy Victoria's ceiling insulation rules, a licensed electrician must complete a pre-installation electrical safety assessment alongside an installer safety assessment before any insulation is laid. Homes with recessed halogen downlights or unsafe wiring are ineligible until those electrical hazards are rectified. Do Victorian rental properties need ceiling insulation from 1 March 2027? Under Victoria's rental minimum energy efficiency standards, rental properties that currently have no ceiling insulation must have at least R5.0 ceiling insulation installed at the start of a new lease from 1 March 2027, unless a regulatory exemption applies. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Energy Rebates for Concession Card Holders in Victoria Energy Rebates for Concession Card Holders in Victoria Victorian Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card, and DVA Gold Card holders receive ongoing percentage discounts off household electricity and winter mains gas bills, and can also access upfront Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) appliance discounts. VEU product pages apply no income test, while owner-occupiers below the Solar Homes household income cap can combine hot water rebates or apply for solar PV support. For free one-on-one help checking missing concessions or payment difficulty support, contact the Victorian Government's Energy Assistance Program. 17.5% Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Department of Families, Fairness and Housing (DFFH) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Ongoing electricity and winter gas bill concessions Households holding a valid Pensioner Concession Card , Health Care Card , or DVA Gold Card can register their card with their energy retailer for two ongoing Victorian concessions: Annual Electricity Concession: 17.5% [source] off household electricity usage and service charges year-round, calculated after the first $171.60 [source] of annual electricity bills ( DFFH — Annual electricity concession ). Winter Gas Concession: 17.5% [source] off mains gas usage and service charges between 1 May and 31 October , calculated after the first $62.40 [source] of winter gas bills ( DFFH — Winter gas concession ). If you switch heating, hot water, and cooking off mains gas completely ( see our Get-Off-Gas Planner ), your gas bills and Winter Gas Concession stop once your gas account closes, while the Annual Electricity Concession continues across your electric load. Both homeowners and Victorian renters whose names are on the energy account can claim these concessions. Appliance upgrade discounts: VEU vs Solar Homes Concession card holders can access appliance upgrades through two separate Victorian programs ( compare VEU vs Solar Homes ): Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU): Energy Victoria’s heating, cooling, and hot water pages apply no household income test ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ; Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ). Watch out for uninvited callers claiming “free pensioner upgrades”—every VEU upgrade still carries a mandatory co-payment, and cold calling is banned ( read our VEU scams guide ). Solar Homes Program: Eligible owner-occupiers with combined household income under $150,000 [source] ( Solar Victoria — Targeted assistance update ) can apply for hot water or rooftop solar PV rebates. Free bill and concession help: Energy Assistance Program The Energy Assistance Program provides free Victorian Government help for concession holders and households experiencing bill stress—checking that your retailer has applied your concessions, comparing energy plans, and arranging payment-difficulty support ( Energy Victoria — Energy Assistance Program ). To check appliance discounts for your home, open the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Does the Victorian Energy Upgrades program have an income test or require a concession card? No. Energy Victoria’s household heating, cooling, and hot water product pages apply no household income test and do not require a concession card to receive a point-of-sale VEU discount. By contrast, the separate Solar Homes program has a household taxable income cap for owner-occupiers—compare both schemes on /victoria/veu-vs-solar-homes/. What happens to my Winter Gas Concession if I switch my home from gas to electric? The Winter Gas Concession applies only to mains gas usage and service charges billed between 1 May and 31 October, so closing your gas account ends gas bills and the gas concession together. Eligible Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card, and DVA Gold Card holders continue to receive the Annual Electricity Concession on their year-round electricity usage and service charges above the annual threshold shown on this page. Where can concession card holders get help with Victorian energy bills? The Victorian Government’s Energy Assistance Program provides free, one-on-one support to help eligible households check missing concessions, compare energy plans, and access retailer payment-difficulty assistance. You can reach the Energy Assistance Program through the official Energy Victoria link in the sources section below. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Draught Proofing (Weather Sealing) Rebate Victoria (VEU) Draught Proofing (Weather Sealing) Rebate Victoria (VEU) Victorian households can access upfront Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) weather sealing discounts through an accredited provider to seal air leaks around doors, windows, exhaust fans, wall vents, chimneys, and evaporative cooler vents. Before booking any draught proofing, check your gas appliances—homes with an open-flued or flueless indoor gas heater or open-flued indoor gas water heater do not qualify because sealing air vents creates a serious carbon monoxide risk. Indicative VEU discounts scale by dwelling type and product warranty length. $700 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Mandatory safety rule first: carbon monoxide and indoor gas heaters Homes with open-flued or flueless indoor gas appliances do not qualify Energy Victoria excludes any home that has an open-flued or flueless gas space heater or an open-flued gas water heater installed indoors from VEU weather sealing ( Energy Victoria — Weather sealing discounts ). Sealing doors, windows, wall vents, and chimneys reduces indoor airflow and can cause dangerous, odourless carbon monoxide to spill into living spaces. If you are unsure what “open-flued” or “flueless” means: Open-flued gas appliance: Draws air for combustion from the room inside your home and vents exhaust gases up a flue or chimney (common in older wall furnaces, gas space heaters, and decorative gas log fires). If exhaust fans run and air gaps are sealed tight, negative pressure can suck exhaust fumes back into the room. Flueless gas heater: Burns gas inside the room with no flue pipe to the outside at all, releasing combustion gases directly indoors. Until an unsafe indoor gas appliance is permanently decommissioned or replaced with an all-electric system, do not seal fixed wall vents or draught-proof the home. In rented properties with gas appliances, Consumer Affairs Victoria also requires a gas safety check before draught proofing ( see rules for Victorian renters ). What VEU weather sealing covers and indicative discounts In an eligible home, an accredited provider’s installer can fit approved weather-sealing products across ( Energy Victoria — Weather sealing discounts ): External doors and windows Self-sealing exhaust fans Unused wall vents and chimneys Evaporative cooler ceiling vents Energy Victoria publishes six indicative household weather sealing examples by dwelling type (apartment, townhouse, or house) and product warranty ( 2-year vs 5-year warranty): Household VEU weather sealing (draught proofing) examples · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 against Weather sealing discounts — Victorian Energy Upgrades (Energy Victoria (DEECA)) ↗ . Indicative. The accredited provider confirms the final amount in your quote. Upgrade scenario Indicative VEU discount Example: apartment, products with a 2-year warranty $70 Example: apartment, 5-year warranty $140 Example: house, 2-year warranty $350 Example: house, 5-year warranty $700 Example: townhouse, 2-year warranty $280 Example: townhouse, 5-year warranty $560 Pairing weather sealing with VEU ceiling insulation helps keep conditioned air inside, and from 1 July 2027 draught proofing becomes part of Victoria’s minimum rental energy efficiency standards at a new lease. Window glazing and local council DIY rebates Two related options sit alongside VEU weather sealing: VEU window glazing discounts: Energy Victoria publishes household window glazing examples of $210 [source] for double glazing and $140 [source] for secondary glazing per 10 m² of treated glass ( Energy Victoria — Window glazing discounts ). Council DIY rebates: Separate from VEU (which requires professional installation through an accredited provider), residents in the City of Casey can apply for a municipal DIY draught-proofing product rebate of up to $200 [source] , limited to one per household ( City of Casey — Home energy rebates ). Check whether your home qualifies for VEU weather sealing in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions What parts of a home can be sealed under VEU weather sealing? Energy Victoria lists weather sealing upgrades covering external doors, windows, exhaust fans, wall vents, chimneys, and evaporative cooler vents using approved draught-proofing products installed by an accredited provider’s installer. Indicative discounts vary between apartments, townhouses, and detached houses and whether the installed products carry a two-year or five-year warranty. Why don’t homes with open-flued or flueless gas heaters qualify for VEU weather sealing? Sealing air vents, chimneys, and door gaps in a home that still operates an open-flued or flueless indoor gas space heater or open-flued indoor gas water heater can starve the burner of ventilation and draw dangerous carbon monoxide back into living rooms. Because of that carbon monoxide risk, Energy Victoria excludes those homes from VEU weather sealing until unsafe gas appliances are removed or replaced. Are there Victorian council rebates for DIY draught-proofing products? Some local councils run separate municipal rebates alongside VEU—for example, the City of Casey offers a household rebate for eligible DIY draught-proofing products, limited to one claim per household. Check our local guide at /victoria/casey/ or your own council’s sustainability page for current opening dates and receipt rules. From 30 September 2026, every household ducted upgrade also carries a mandatory minimum customer co-payment, and your property must be more than two years old. Always engage a VEU accredited provider before decommissioning your existing ducted gas unit. up to $2,520 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Ducted gas replacement discounts by system size (10 kW, 16 kW, 22.4 kW) Energy Victoria publishes three household ducted gas replacement examples depending on the capacity of the new ducted reverse-cycle system ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ). Because the largest figure applies only to a 22.4 kW whole-home installation, compare all three sizes side by side: Household ducted gas to ducted reverse-cycle VEU discounts · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 against Heating and cooling discounts — Victorian Energy Upgrades (Energy Victoria (DEECA)) ↗ . Indicative. The accredited provider confirms the final amount in your quote. Upgrade scenario Indicative VEU discount Replace a ducted gas heater with a 10 kW ducted reverse-cycle system up to $2,520 Replace a ducted gas heater with a 16 kW ducted reverse-cycle system up to $4,200 Replace a ducted gas heater with a 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system up to $5,530 If you prefer zoning individual rooms rather than installing a new central ducted unit, compare our ducted gas to split systems and multi-split guide , or review every heating scenario on our Air Conditioner Rebate Victoria guide . What is the minimum you must pay? Under Victorian Energy Upgrades Specifications version 25.0, Part 6 ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ; Energy Victoria — Industry specifications ), from 30 September 2026 the mandatory minimum customer co-payment for any household ducted reverse-cycle air conditioner is at least $3,000 (including GST) [source] per installed product (increased from at least $1,000 (including GST) [source] prior to 30 September 2026). Even where a large ducted replacement attracts a substantial certificate discount, the accredited provider cannot reduce your out-of-pocket payment below at least $3,000 (including GST) [source] . Read more in our guide to the VEU minimum co-payment . Annual running-cost savings and eligibility rules Energy Victoria’s heating and cooling product page estimates that replacing a ducted gas heater with an efficient ducted reverse-cycle system saves households up to $1,140 [source] a year on energy bills. To meet VEU household eligibility rules: Building age: Your home must be more than 2 years old when replacing an existing heating system. Approved product and warranty: The ducted reverse-cycle unit must be listed on the VEU Register of Products and carry at least a 5-year household warranty . Provider before work starts: You must use a VEU accredited provider, or a licensed installer working with one, before disconnecting your old gas unit—see the VEU timing and decommissioning rules . Can renters and landlords upgrade ducted gas heating? Private rental homes are eligible for VEU heating and cooling discounts when the tenant and rental provider work together and the landlord gives written permission before work starts. From 1 March 2027 , when a fixed heater in a rental home’s main living area breaks down and cannot be repaired, the rental provider must replace it with an efficient reverse-cycle air conditioner. Check your property in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions How do I know whether my home needs a 10 kW, 16 kW, or 22.4 kW ducted system? Energy Victoria publishes indicative ducted replacement examples at 10 kW, 16 kW, and 22.4 kW capacities, and recommends asking an installer for an on-site home assessment so the unit matches your floor area, insulation, and ductwork. Installing an oversized unit can increase electricity use, and your accredited provider confirms the exact capacity and discount in your quote. Is there a minimum I have to pay for a ducted system? Yes. Under Victorian Energy Upgrades Specifications version 25.0 (Part 6), every household heating and cooling upgrade requires a minimum customer co-payment that took effect on 30 September 2026, so the discount cannot cover the full cost of the system. Check the current co-payment tiers by system type in the minimum customer co-payment section at /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/#the-minimum-you-pay-from-30-september-2026. Are rental properties eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades discounts? Yes, rental properties in Victoria can access VEU discounts for approved reverse-cycle air conditioners and hot water upgrades, provided the building is more than two years old when replacing an existing system. Renters must have the landlord's approval before any heating, cooling, or hot water installation takes place. From 1 March 2027, new rental minimum efficiency standards also apply when systems fail or at the start of a new lease. Can I claim a Victorian Energy Upgrades discount after my system is already installed? Generally no. Energy Victoria advises that you must contact an accredited provider (or use an installer working with one) before buying or installing your system. Retrospective discounts after installation work has started are typically not possible. See our guide on /victoria/reverse-cycle-vs-gas-heater/ for how the timing rule works. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Replace Ducted Gas With Split Systems: VEU Discount Replace Ducted Gas With Split Systems: VEU Discount Yes, Victorian households can decommission an existing ducted gas heater and install either multiple single split systems or a multi-split reverse-cycle system under the VEU program. Energy Victoria publishes separate indicative figures for four single splits versus a multi-split system, and VEU Specifications version 25 revised both multi-split incentive calculations and minimum customer co-payments from 30 September 2026. Your accredited provider confirms the exact discount in your written quote before work starts. up to $2,520 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Four single splits vs one multi-split: indicative VEU discounts Many Victorian homeowners decommissioning an ageing underfloor or ceiling ducted gas heater choose room-by-room split heads instead of new ductwork. Energy Victoria lists two indicative household examples when replacing a ducted gas heater ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ): Replacing ducted gas with 4 single split systems (1 × 8 kW plus 3 × 3 kW): up to $2,520 [source] . Replacing ducted gas with a multi-split system (1 × 10 kW outdoor unit): up to $2,940 [source] . Ducted gas to split and multi-split VEU scenarios · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 against Heating and cooling discounts — Victorian Energy Upgrades (Energy Victoria (DEECA)) ↗ . Indicative. The accredited provider confirms the final amount in your quote. Upgrade scenario Indicative VEU discount Replace a ducted gas heater with 4 single split systems up to $2,520 Replace a ducted gas heater with a multi-split reverse-cycle system up to $2,940 If you also want to compare keeping whole-home ductwork, see our ducted gas to ducted reverse-cycle guide , or if you are replacing a single wall furnace see our gas room heater to split-system guide . Multi-split product rules and 30 September 2026 calculation updates Under VEU Specifications version 25.0 ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ; Energy Victoria — Industry specifications ): Revised multi-split calculations: Version 25.0 revised multi-split incentive calculations for upgrades from 30 September 2026 . Because certificate counts depend on the exact indoor and outdoor model ratings and postcode climate zone, your accredited provider confirms the final discount amount in your quote. Same manufacturer requirement: All indoor units connected to a multi-split outdoor unit must be from the same manufacturer as the outdoor unit. Standard household rules: The property must be more than 2 years old, products must carry at least a 5-year household warranty, and an accredited provider must be engaged before decommissioning the ducted gas heater. Minimum customer co-payments from 30 September 2026 Your minimum out-of-pocket co-payment per installed product depends on whether you choose individual single splits or a multi-split system: Split and multi-split minimum co-payments (from 30 Sep 2026) · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 against Victorian Energy Upgrades Specifications 2018 Version 25.0 (PDF) (Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action (DEECA)) ↗ . Indicative. The accredited provider confirms the final amount in your quote. Frequently asked questions Which gives a larger VEU discount when replacing ducted gas: four single splits or a multi-split? In Energy Victoria's published household examples, decommissioning a ducted gas heater for a multi-split system with a 10 kW outdoor unit has a slightly higher indicative maximum discount than installing four separate single split systems, though the minimum customer co-payment rules also differ by system configuration and capacity. Compare both rows in the scenario table on /victoria/ducted-gas-to-split-systems/. Can I mix indoor and outdoor unit brands on a multi-split VEU upgrade? No. Under Victorian Energy Upgrades Specifications version 25.0, all indoor units connected to a multi-split system must come from the same manufacturer as the outdoor unit, and the product combination must be listed on the VEU Register of Products with at least a five-year household warranty. What minimum co-payment applies to split and multi-split upgrades from 30 September 2026? Under VEU Specifications version 25.0 (Part 6), the mandatory minimum customer co-payment depends on whether you install individual single split systems or a multi-split system, and whether total rated cooling capacity is below 10 kW or 10 kW and above. Check the exact GST-inclusive co-payment table on /victoria/ducted-gas-to-split-systems/. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Electric Heater to Reverse Cycle Rebate Victoria Electric Heater to Reverse Cycle Rebate Victoria Yes, Victorian households replacing fixed electric resistance heating with an approved reverse-cycle air conditioner can access a VEU point-of-sale discount. Energy Victoria lists separate indicative discounts for replacing a hard-wired electric room heater with a split system versus replacing a central electric resistance ducted heater with a ducted reverse-cycle system. Plug-in portable electric heaters do not count as an eligible existing system. up to $840 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Hard-wired panel or slab heater vs central electric ducted heating Homes in regional towns, apartments, and older Melbourne suburbs without mains gas often run fixed electric resistance heaters (such as hard-wired wall panel heaters, in-slab heating, or central electric ducted furnaces). Energy Victoria publishes two household electric-replacement scenarios ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ): Hard-wired electric resistance room heater to a 3–9 kW split system: up to $840 [source] . Central electric resistance ducted heater to a 10–22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system: up to $5,460 [source] . Compare these against gas-replacement figures on our Air Conditioner Rebate Victoria guide and our ducted gas to ducted reverse-cycle guide . Do portable plug-in heaters count? No. Portable plug-in fan, oil-column, or radiant heaters are not listed as an eligible current heating system on Energy Victoria’s heating and cooling table. Only fixed, hard-wired electric resistance room heaters or central electric resistance ducted heaters qualify for the electric-replacement scenarios above; if no fixed heater is decommissioned, the smaller no-decommission split or ducted scenario applies instead. Minimum co-payments and eligibility checks Under VEU Specifications version 25.0 ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ), mandatory minimum customer co-payments apply per installed product from 30 September 2026 : Single non-ducted split system below 10 kW: at least $200 (including GST) [source] . Any ducted reverse-cycle system: at least $3,000 (including GST) [source] . Your home must be more than 2 years old when replacing an existing heater, the new reverse-cycle unit must carry at least a 5-year household warranty , and you must engage a VEU accredited provider before decommissioning the existing electric heater. Read more on VEU minimum co-payments , explore heating running-cost comparisons , or test your upgrade in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Do plug-in portable electric heaters count for a VEU replacement discount? No. Energy Victoria's household heating and cooling table only lists hard-wired electric resistance room heaters and central electric resistance ducted heaters as eligible electric systems to replace. If you only use portable plug-in heaters, any new reverse-cycle unit falls under the smaller scenario where no fixed heater is decommissioned. What is the difference between replacing a hard-wired room heater and a central electric ducted heater? Replacing a hard-wired electric resistance room heater (such as a fixed wall panel or slab heater) with a 3 to 9 kW split system falls under the non-ducted replacement scenario, whereas replacing a central electric resistance ducted heater with a 10 to 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system falls under the ducted scenario and carries the ducted minimum co-payment. Compare both figures on /victoria/electric-heater-to-reverse-cycle/. Is there a minimum I have to pay for a ducted system? Yes. Under Victorian Energy Upgrades Specifications version 25.0 (Part 6), every household heating and cooling upgrade requires a minimum customer co-payment that took effect on 30 September 2026, so the discount cannot cover the full cost of the system. Check the current co-payment tiers by system type in the minimum customer co-payment section at /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/#the-minimum-you-pay-from-30-september-2026. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Electric Hot Water to Heat Pump Rebate Victoria Electric Hot Water to Heat Pump Rebate Victoria Replacing an inefficient electric storage water heater in Victoria attracts a higher indicative VEU discount than replacing a mains gas system, whether you choose an approved heat pump or a solar-boosted water heater. Energy Victoria notes that heat pump water heaters use significantly less electricity than standard electric resistance tanks and can run on timers during solar PV hours. Your building must be at least two years old, and an accredited provider confirms your quote before work starts. $630 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 VEU discounts when replacing an electric hot water system On Energy Victoria’s hot water discounts page ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ), replacing an inefficient electric resistance water heater in a building at least two years old carries two indicative household VEU figures: Inefficient electric water heater to an approved heat pump: $630 [source] . Inefficient electric water heater to an approved solar-boosted system: $910 [source] . VEU discounts for replacing an inefficient electric water heater · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 against Hot water system discounts — Victorian Energy Upgrades (Energy Victoria (DEECA)) ↗ . Indicative. The accredited provider confirms the final amount in your quote. Upgrade scenario Indicative VEU discount Replace an inefficient electric hot water system with a heat pump $630 Replace an inefficient electric hot water system with a solar-boosted hot water system $910 Compare these with mains gas replacement figures on our Heat Pump Rebate Victoria guide , or explore collector-based systems on our Solar Hot Water Rebate Victoria guide . Separate Solar Homes hot water rebate and Federal STCs Alongside the VEU point-of-sale discount, two separate programs may apply depending on your household and product: Solar Homes hot water rebate: up to $1,000 [source] (or up to $1,400 [source] for an eligible locally made product) from Solar Victoria ( Solar Victoria — Hot water rebate ). You must be an owner-occupier within Solar Victoria’s income and property value caps, replace a system at least 3 years old, and get pre-approval before installation. Read how VEU and Solar Homes compare . Federal STCs: Eligible air-source heat pumps with a tank capacity under 425 litres on the Clean Energy Regulator register also create Small-scale Technology Certificates ( CER — Solar water heaters and air source heat pumps ). We show the VEU and Solar Homes amounts separately because Solar Victoria calculates its rebate on the remaining price after STCs and VEECs are deducted, and your accredited provider confirms your exact out-of-pocket quote. How much less electricity does a heat pump use, and can it run on solar PV? According to Energy Victoria, heat pump water heaters use up to 75% [source] less electricity than a standard electric storage system. Energy Victoria’s consumer factsheet ( VEU Water Heating Consumer Factsheet PDF ) also highlights that many heat pumps include built-in timers so the unit runs during the middle of the day using electricity from your rooftop solar panels. If you plan to heat water only once a day during solar hours, ask your installer whether you should step up a tank size ( check our heat pump hot water size guide ), or test your setup in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions How much less electricity does a heat pump use compared to an electric storage tank? Energy Victoria states that heat pump water heaters use a fraction of the electricity of a conventional electric resistance storage water heater because they move heat from the air rather than generating heat directly with an element. Check the published percentage figure and VEU discount table on /victoria/electric-hot-water-to-heat-pump/. Can I run a heat pump water heater off my rooftop solar panels? Yes. Energy Victoria's water heating consumer factsheet notes that many heat pump models include built-in timers so you can heat water during sunny daytime hours using your solar PV output, though setting a daytime-only timer can require a slightly larger storage tank. Should I replace an electric hot water tank with a heat pump or a solar-boosted system? Both options are eligible on the VEU Register of Products when replacing an inefficient electric water heater in a building at least two years old. A solar-boosted system uses roof-mounted collectors and has a higher indicative VEU discount, while a heat pump needs no roof plumbing and can still pair with existing solar PV panels via a timer. When you check ceiling insulation, the VEU postcode table sets whether your postcode is listed as metropolitan or regional and its climatic region. Your postcode stays in your browser and nothing is sent anywhere. Can I claim a Victorian Energy Upgrades discount after my system is already installed? Generally no. Energy Victoria advises that you must contact an accredited provider (or use an installer working with one) before buying or installing your system. Retrospective discounts after installation work has started are typically not possible. See our guide on /victoria/reverse-cycle-vs-gas-heater/ for how the timing rule works. Why does the air conditioner discount vary so much between homes? The Victorian Energy Upgrades discount is calculated from the greenhouse gas savings of your specific upgrade. Replacing a whole-home ducted gas heater with a high-capacity ducted reverse-cycle system creates far more certificates than replacing a single room gas heater or installing a split system without decommissioning an existing heater. Compare the full scenario tables on /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/. Why is the VEU heat pump discount different when replacing gas versus electric hot water? Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades methodology, replacing an inefficient electric resistance water heater saves more calculated emissions than replacing a mains gas water heater, so the point-of-sale discount differs between the two scenarios. Check the exact figures for both replacement types on /victoria/heat-pump-rebate/. Are rental properties eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades discounts? Yes, rental properties in Victoria can access VEU discounts for approved reverse-cycle air conditioners and hot water upgrades, provided the building is more than two years old when replacing an existing system. Renters must have the landlord's approval before any heating, cooling, or hot water installation takes place. From 1 March 2027, new rental minimum efficiency standards also apply when systems fail or at the start of a new lease.
