Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria How to Find a VEU Accredited Provider in Victoria How to Find a VEU Accredited Provider in Victoria Only businesses accredited by the Essential Services Commission—known as VEU accredited providers—can create Victorian Energy Efficiency Certificates and apply an upfront VEU discount to your quote. If you prefer your own local plumber or electrician, they must partner with an accredited provider before any installation work begins. You can look up accredited providers by Victorian region on Energy Victoria's product pages, use the state-owned Easy Electric SEC free quote-matching tool, or check council-backed home energy programs. By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Accredited providers vs local licensed installers Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program, only accredited providers can apply the upfront VEU discount and register certificates ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ; Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ). Some large heating, cooling, and hot water companies are both the licensed installer and the VEU accredited provider. Many independent plumbers and electricians are not accredited providers themselves—if you hire your own tradesperson, they must already partner with an accredited provider before work starts ( see how VEU quotes and consent rules work ). Remember that unsolicited cold calling and doorknocking are banned under VEU ( how to spot VEU scams and cold calls ). Energy Victoria’s regional provider lists Energy Victoria publishes downloadable lists of participating accredited providers on each VEU product page, grouped into six Victorian regions ( Energy Victoria — Find an accredited provider by region ): Greater Melbourne Barwon South West Gippsland Grampians Hume Loddon Mallee Energy Victoria notes that not every accredited provider offers every VEU upgrade activity at present —check the list on the specific product page (hot water, heating and cooling, ceiling insulation, induction cooktops, or weather sealing) that matches your job. Easy Electric SEC (free state-owned quote tool) Alongside Energy Victoria’s directories, the Victorian Government’s state-owned State Electricity Commission (SEC) operates Easy Electric SEC —a free online tool that helps Victorian households plan electric upgrades and connects you with SEC-endorsed installers ( SEC Victoria — Going electric at home with Easy Electric SEC ; SEC Victoria — Easy Electric SEC FAQs ). According to the SEC’s published FAQs, once you choose to request quotes through Easy Electric SEC, an SEC-endorsed installer contacts you within one business day , at no cost for using the SEC matching tool. Council-backed home energy programs Several Victorian councils also connect residents with vetted installers or home energy advice—for example, the council-backed program serving the City of Whittlesea ( Home Energy Program — City of Whittlesea ) and sustainable homes initiatives in Yarra Ranges ( Yarra Ranges Council — Sustainable homes ). Before contacting any provider, check which VEU scenario fits your home in our Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions What is the difference between a VEU accredited provider and a licensed installer? Only businesses accredited by the Essential Services Commission (accredited providers) can create Victorian Energy Efficiency Certificates and apply an upfront VEU discount. Many local plumbers and electricians are not accredited providers themselves, so if you choose your own tradesperson they must partner with an accredited provider before any installation work begins. What is Easy Electric SEC? Easy Electric SEC is a free online quote-matching tool operated by the Victorian Government’s state-owned State Electricity Commission (SEC) that connects households with SEC-endorsed installers. According to the SEC, an endorsed installer contacts you within one business day after you submit your details through its tool. Do Victorian councils help residents find vetted upgrade installers? Yes. Several Victorian councils participate in council-backed home energy programs or route residents to vetted upgrade services, including programs in the City of Whittlesea and Yarra Ranges Shire. Check our local area guides as they roll out or visit your council’s sustainability page. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Frankston Air Conditioner & Heat Pump Rebates (VEU) Frankston Air Conditioner & Heat Pump Rebates (VEU) Homeowners, landlords, and renters in Frankston City Council postcodes can access upfront Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discounts when replacing gas or electric heating and hot water units with approved reverse-cycle air conditioners or heat pumps. Indicative discounts vary depending on whether you decommission a room gas heater, a ducted gas system, or an electric/gas hot water unit. Engage an accredited provider before any work starts. $630 to $1,610 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Local context for Frankston (Frankston City Council) Postcodes covered on this page: 3198, 3199, 3200, 3910, 3911 Frankston City Council's Climate Change Strategy promotes household energy upgrades and switching from gas to efficient electric appliances across Frankston, Seaford, and Langwarrin. [Frankston City Council] Bureau of Meteorology bayside climate data shows winter minimums around 6.5°C to 7.0°C and warm summer peaks, making dual heating-and-cooling reverse-cycle systems well suited. [Bureau of Meteorology (BoM)] Post-1970s brick-veneer homes across Frankston South, Karingal, and Langwarrin commonly have ducted gas or wall furnaces eligible for VEU decommissioning discounts. [Energy Victoria (DEECA)] Coastal installations in Frankston and Seaford still require an approved VEU product with at least a 5-year household warranty. Under Energy Victoria’s VEU heating and cooling schedule: Single split system (3–9 kW) replacing a room gas heater: indicative discount of $630 to $1,610 [source] . 16 kW ducted reverse-cycle replacing a ducted gas heater: indicative discount of up to $4,200 [source] . 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle replacing a ducted gas heater: indicative discount of up to $5,530 [source] . Remember that your installer must work with a VEU accredited provider before disconnecting your old gas heater so pre-installation photos and compliance evidence can be recorded. Heat pump hot water discounts in Frankston When replacing an existing hot water unit in a building at least two years old: Replacing an inefficient electric water heater with a heat pump: indicative discount of $630 [source] . Replacing an inefficient mains gas water heater with a heat pump: indicative discount of $560 [source] . Minimum customer co-contribution: $200 [source] . From 1 March 2027 , existing mains gas water heaters that reach the end of their life in Frankston homes must generally be replaced with an efficient electric system. Read the full details in our 1 March 2027 Gas Hot Water Rule guide . Participating installers covering Frankston We do not yet have a signed partner installer covering Frankston postcodes. Until partner agreements for this area are finalised, you can search Energy Victoria's official accredited provider directory directly or check your upgrade scenario with our Victoria Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Why does the air conditioner discount vary so much between homes? The Victorian Energy Upgrades discount is calculated from the greenhouse gas savings of your specific upgrade. Replacing a whole-home ducted gas heater with a high-capacity ducted reverse-cycle system creates far more certificates than replacing a single room gas heater or installing a split system without decommissioning an existing heater. Compare the full scenario tables on /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/. Can I claim a Victorian Energy Upgrades discount after my system is already installed? Generally no. Energy Victoria advises that you must contact an accredited provider (or use an installer working with one) before buying or installing your system. Retrospective discounts after installation work has started are typically not possible. See our guide on /victoria/reverse-cycle-vs-gas-heater/ for how the timing rule works. What happens on 1 March 2027 when a gas hot water system breaks down? From 1 March 2027, when a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing Victorian home reaches the end of its life and needs replacing, it generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas unit and must be replaced with an electric alternative such as a heat pump or solar-boosted system. Exemptions apply for certain technical constraints, and bottled LPG systems are not affected. Read the full details on /victoria/gas-to-electric-hot-water-2027/. Quote requests are not open yet We're not taking quote requests yet. To get a discount now, contact an accredited provider from Energy Victoria's list: Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts and providers ↗ Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts and providers ↗ Not sure which scenario applies to your home? Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Gas Cooktop to Induction Rebate Victoria (VEU 2026) Gas Cooktop to Induction Rebate Victoria (VEU 2026) Victorian households replacing an existing gas cooktop with an eligible built-in or freestanding induction cooktop can claim a VEU discount per product. Unlike heating or hot water upgrades, the induction cooktop process lets you check eligibility first, buy an eligible cooktop from a retailer, and send your invoice to a participating accredited provider while arranging installation separately. Existing homes are not required to remove gas cooktops under Victoria's 2027 rules. $140 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 How to claim the VEU induction cooktop discount Confirm your home and current cooktop meet VEU rules. Check that your home was built at least two years ago, currently has a gas cooktop to replace, and has not previously claimed a VEU induction cooktop discount. Verify the cooktop dimensions, zones, and provider terms before buying. Choose a built-in or freestanding induction cooktop (not portable) measuring at least 550 mm by 380 mm with three or more cooking zones and at least a two-year warranty, and check a participating accredited provider's evidence checklist. Buy the eligible cooktop and keep your itemised invoice. Purchase the eligible induction cooktop and retain the tax invoice showing the brand, model, purchase date, and amount paid. Submit your invoice to an accredited provider and arrange licensed installation. Send the purchase invoice and required evidence to the participating VEU accredited provider to claim the discount, and arrange installation and gas capping separately with licensed tradespeople. How much is the VEU induction cooktop discount? According to Energy Victoria ( Energy Victoria — Induction cooktop discounts ), the indicative household VEU discount for replacing a gas cooktop with an eligible induction cooktop is $140 [source] per product, calculated on a certificate price basis of $70 [source] ( see how VEEC certificate prices work ). Under VEU Specifications version 25.0 ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ), each induction cooktop product also carries a mandatory minimum customer co-payment of at least $200 (including GST) [source] . How the buy-first claim process differs from other VEU upgrades For air conditioners and hot water systems, you must engage an accredited provider before purchasing anything. Induction cooktops follow a different workflow on Energy Victoria’s product page: Check eligibility first: Confirm your home, existing gas cooktop, and chosen model meet all VEU criteria, and review a participating accredited provider’s claim requirements. Buy the cooktop: Purchase the eligible induction cooktop from a retailer. Send the invoice to an accredited provider: Submit your tax invoice and required evidence to the accredited provider to receive the discount. Arrange installation separately: Have a licensed electrician wire the dedicated induction circuit and a licensed gasfitter cap the old gas cooktop connection. Which cooktops and homes qualify? Every one of Energy Victoria’s criteria must be met: Replacing gas: Must replace a current gas cooktop in a Victorian home built at least 2 years ago . One claim limit: You must not have previously claimed an induction cooktop discount ( see rules on claiming VEU more than once ). Built-in or freestanding only: Portable plug-in benchtop induction units are not eligible. Minimum size, zones, and warranty: At least 550 × 380 mm , 3 or more cooking zones , and at least a 2-year warranty . Disconnecting mains gas completely Existing Victorian homes have no legal requirement to replace gas cooktops ( Energy Victoria — Existing residential buildings ). However, for households that have already switched heating and hot water (for example via our gas hot water to heat pump guide ), replacing a gas cooktop is often the final step to abolishing the gas meter—which Energy Victoria notes could save about $350 to $400 [source] per year in avoided gas supply charges ( see our Get-Off-Gas Planner ). Check your cooktop and other appliances in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Do I buy an induction cooktop first and claim the VEU discount afterwards? Yes. Unlike heating or hot water upgrades, Energy Victoria's induction cooktop process lets you check that your home and chosen model meet the rules, purchase the eligible cooktop, and then submit your purchase invoice to a participating accredited provider to claim the discount, while arranging licensed installation separately. Which induction cooktops qualify for the Victorian Energy Upgrades discount? To be eligible on Energy Victoria's current rules, the induction cooktop must replace an existing gas cooktop in a home built at least two years ago, have not been previously claimed at that home, be a built-in or freestanding unit (not portable), measure at least 550 mm by 380 mm, have three or more cooking zones, and carry at least a two-year warranty. Do existing Victorian homes have to remove gas cooktops, or is switching optional? Switching from a gas cooktop to induction in an existing Victorian home is completely voluntary. Victoria's building electrification rules do not require existing homeowners to replace working or broken gas cooktops, though removing your final gas appliance lets you abolish the gas meter and avoid ongoing gas supply charges. /victoria/gas-hot-water-ban-exemptions/.text: Victoria 2027 Gas Hot Water Rule Exemptions (Reg 45E) | Household Rebates Skip to main content Independent guide run by Agenor Services Pty Ltd (ABN 29 644 447 263). Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Victoria 2027 Gas Hot Water Rule Exemptions (Reg 45E) Victoria 2027 Gas Hot Water Rule Exemptions (Reg 45E) Victoria's 1 March 2027 mains gas water heater replacement rule includes narrow technical, temporary, and transitional exemptions under regulation 45E of the Building and Plumbing Amendment Regulations 2025. Technical exemptions cover properties without suitable indoor or outdoor space, Class 2 buildings or pools on a centralised gas system, main switchboard or distribution board alterations, and electricity network augmentation beyond a standard connection. This page is a plain-English summary, not legal advice, and your licensed plumber assesses whether an exemption applies. By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Plain-English summary (not legal advice) From 1 March 2027 , regulation 45E restricts licensed plumbers from installing a mains gas water heater to replace an existing water heater in an established Victorian home unless a listed exemption applies. The authoritative legislation is published on Victorian Legislation ( Building and Plumbing Amendment Regulations 2025 (SR 140/2025) on legislation.vic.gov.au ), with the section text reproduced on AustLII ( SR 140/2025 reg 6 — regulation 45E text (AustLII) ) and summarised in the Victoria Government Gazette ( Victoria Government Gazette S654 (2025) ). Important notice: not legal advice This guide is a plain-English consumer summary and is not legal advice . Under regulation 45E, compliance rests on the licensed plumber (facing a maximum penalty of 20 penalty units for an unlawful installation), and your plumber determines whether an exemption applies to your property. Technical and property exemptions — regulation 45E(3) Under regulation 45E(3) ( Regulation 45E(3) text ), a mains gas replacement is exempt where installing a non-mains-gas water heater is prevented by one of the following: Insufficient indoor or outdoor space: There is not enough space inside the building and no suitable outdoor space to install a compliant non-mains-gas alternative. Centralised Class 2 building or pool system: The water heater serves a Class 2 building (such as an apartment block—see our apartments and units guide ) or a swimming pool connected to a centralised gas hot water system. Unlawful under another law: Installing the electric or solar alternative would breach another law or planning requirement. Switchboard or distribution board alteration: Installing the non-mains-gas system would require altering the property’s main switchboard or distribution board ( Victoria Government Gazette S654 ). Network augmentation: Installing the system would require electricity supply network augmentation beyond a basic or standard connection. Operational and transitional exemptions — regulation 45E(4) and 45E(5) Regulation 45E(4) exempts three operational situations ( Regulation 45E(4) text ; Victoria Government Gazette S654 ): Temporary disconnection and reconnection of an existing gas water heater (for example, during renovations). No-electricity like-for-like gas replacement where the gas water heater requires no electricity connection to operate. Warranty replacement during the manufacturer, supplier, or installer warranty period. Regulation 45E(5) exempts three transitional situations ( Regulation 45E(5) text ): Pre-March 2027 contracts: Work completed within 3 months after 1 March 2027 under a contract signed before 1 March 2027—see what happens if your gas hot water breaks before or after March 2027 . Prior building work: Eligible building work already underway under section 10(1) or 10(2) before 1 March 2027. Rectification orders: Work carried out under a rectification order issued before 1 March 2027. For most standalone homes where an outdoor heat pump fits without a switchboard alteration, compare Victoria’s 2027 gas-to-electric hot water overview , gas-to-heat-pump VEU discounts , and our Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions What if my home or apartment has no suitable space or uses centralised gas hot water? Under regulation 45E(3), exemptions apply where there is insufficient indoor space or no suitable outdoor space for an electric water heater, or where a Class 2 apartment building or swimming pool is served by a centralised gas hot water system. Is there an exemption if an electric water heater requires a main switchboard or network upgrade? Yes. Regulation 45E(3) includes exemptions where installing an electric water heater would require altering the main switchboard or a distribution board, or augmenting the electricity distribution network beyond a basic or standard connection. Who decides whether a 2027 gas hot water exemption applies to my property? Your licensed plumber assesses your property against regulation 45E and carries the statutory obligation (with a penalty of 20 penalty units for a breach). Our guide is a plain-English summary of the regulation text, not legal advice. /victoria/gas-hot-water-broken-before-or.text: Broken Gas Hot Water Victoria: Before or After March 2027 | Household Rebates Skip to main content Independent guide run by Agenor Services Pty Ltd (ABN 29 644 447 263). Not a government website. Installers may pay us for enquiries — how we're paid . Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Broken Gas Hot Water Victoria: Before or After March 2027 Broken Gas Hot Water Victoria: Before or After March 2027 Before 1 March 2027, a broken mains gas hot water system in an existing Victorian home can still be replaced with gas, though upgrading early to a heat pump or electric-boosted solar unit accesses VEU discounts. From 1 March 2027, replacing an existing mains gas water heater—including a gas pool heater—with another mains gas heater is no longer allowed unless a specific regulatory exemption applies. Transitional rules exempt work completed within 3 months after 1 March 2027 under a contract signed before 1 March 2027, as well as warranty replacements and bottled LPG systems. By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Before 1 March 2027 vs from 1 March 2027 Under Victoria’s building and plumbing standards for existing residential buildings ( Energy Victoria — Existing residential buildings ; Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ): Before 1 March 2027: There is no ban on repairing a mains gas water heater or replacing a failed unit with another gas heater, although switching to an approved electric heat pump or solar hot water system lets you access point-of-sale discounts—see our gas hot water to heat pump guide . From 1 March 2027: When a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing home breaks down and needs replacement, it cannot be replaced with another mains gas water heater unless an exemption applies. Repairing a serviceable existing gas unit remains allowed. Read the broader policy timeline in Victoria’s 2027 gas-to-electric hot water guide . This page is a plain-English summary, not legal advice; your licensed plumber confirms how the regulations apply to your job. Transitional contracts and warranty replacements Regulation 45E sets out narrow cases where a mains gas water heater replacement can still proceed on or after 1 March 2027 ( Building and Plumbing Amendment Regulations 2025 — reg 45E text (AustLII) ): Contract signed before 1 March 2027: Work carried out within 3 months after 1 March 2027 under a contract signed with the owner before 1 March 2027 is exempt. Warranty replacement: Replacing a defective gas water heater during the manufacturer, supplier, or installer warranty period is exempt. Technical and building exemptions: Limited space, centralised Class 2 apartment systems, switchboard alterations, or network augmentation exemptions are covered in detail on Victoria’s 2027 gas hot water exemptions . What about LPG, gas heating, cooking, and rental homes? Bottled LPG: Homes running on bottled LPG rather than reticulated mains gas are not affected by the 1 March 2027 mains gas replacement rule ( Planning Victoria — Victoria's Gas Substitution Roadmap ). Gas space heating and cooktops: Existing gas heaters and gas cooktops in owner-occupied homes do not have to be removed when your hot water unit fails ( Energy Victoria — Existing residential buildings ). Rental properties: From 1 March 2027 , when a hot water heater in a Victorian rental property fails beyond repair, the rental provider must replace it with an efficient electric heat pump or electric-boosted solar water heater ( Energy Victoria — Energy efficiency for rental properties ). To plan paperwork and compliance certificates for an urgent swap, read how long a VEU hot water upgrade takes and check your setup in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions What if I sign a hot water replacement contract before 1 March 2027? Under regulation 45E(5) of the Plumbing Regulations (inserted by SR 140/2025), transitional work carried out within three months after 1 March 2027 under a contract signed with the owner before 1 March 2027 is exempt from the mains gas replacement ban. Can a faulty gas water heater still be replaced under warranty after 1 March 2027? Yes. Regulation 45E(4) exempts replacing a gas water heater during the manufacturer, supplier, or installer warranty period, and repairing an existing gas water heater also remains permitted. Does the 1 March 2027 replacement rule affect bottled LPG, gas heaters, or gas cooktops? No for owner-occupied homes. Victoria's Gas Substitution Roadmap confirms bottled LPG water heaters are not affected, and Energy Victoria confirms existing residential buildings can keep or replace gas space heaters and gas cooktops (though separate minimum standards apply to rental properties when a main living area heater fails). Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Gas Hot Water to Heat Pump Rebate Victoria (2026) Gas Hot Water to Heat Pump Rebate Victoria (2026) Replacing an inefficient mains gas water heater with an approved heat pump in Victoria qualifies for a point-of-sale VEU discount, and eligible owner-occupiers can stack the Solar Homes hot water rebate plus Federal STCs on top. Your home must be at least two years old, the product must carry at least a five-year warranty, and a minimum customer contribution applies. Always contact a VEU accredited provider (and get Solar Homes pre-approval if claiming both) before starting installation. $560 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 How VEU, Solar Homes, and STCs stack on a gas-to-heat-pump swap When replacing an inefficient mains gas hot water system with an air-source heat pump, three separate incentives can reduce your upfront cost ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ; Solar Victoria — Hot water rebate ; Clean Energy Regulator — Air source heat pumps ): Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) gas-to-heat-pump discount: indicative $560 [source] in a building at least 2 years old, with at least a 5-year warranty and a minimum customer contribution of $200 [source] . Federal STCs: heat pumps with a volumetric capacity under 425 litres listed on the Clean Energy Regulator register create Small-scale Technology Certificates, usually deducted upfront on your quote. Solar Homes hot water rebate: up to $1,000 [source] ( up to $1,400 [source] for an eligible locally made product), covering 50% [source] of the purchase price calculated after STCs and VEECs are deducted. Available to owner-occupiers with combined household income below $150,000 [source] , property value below $3 million [source] , and an existing water heater at least 3 years old . Energy Victoria lists the combined VEU plus Solar Homes reduction as up to $1,560 [source] , or up to $1,960 [source] with an eligible locally made product, and estimates annual bill savings of around $400 [source] a year. Compare all hot water scenarios on our Heat Pump Rebate Victoria hub and read how VEU and Solar Homes differ . Does bottled LPG count? VEU Specifications Part 3 ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ) covers gas or LPG water heaters, but Energy Victoria publishes only a mains gas figure on its consumer table, so the accredited provider confirms the discount for an LPG replacement. Practical swap checklist: placement, noise, frost, and tank sizing Switching from an instantaneous gas wall unit or gas storage tank to a heat pump involves a few practical site checks: Outdoor airflow and clearance: Air-source heat pumps draw warmth from surrounding air and discharge cool air, so they need clear outdoor ventilation rather than a sealed cupboard. Noise and neighbours: Because a heat pump runs a fan and compressor while heating, ask your installer to place it away from bedroom windows and neighbour boundaries. Winter and frost performance: Ask for a model rated for your Victorian climate zone so cold winter mornings do not reduce recovery speed. Tank size and 2027 planning: Match your storage volume to household size and shower habits ( see our heat pump hot water size guide ). Remember that from 1 March 2027 , failed mains gas water heaters in existing homes generally must be replaced with an electric unit—see our 1 March 2027 gas hot water rule guide , and check your home in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Can I combine the VEU hot water discount, the Solar Homes rebate, and Federal STCs? Yes, where you meet each program's rules. Eligible heat pumps under 425 litres on the Clean Energy Regulator register can receive Federal Small-scale Technology Certificates (STCs) alongside Victorian Energy Upgrades VEECs, and Solar Victoria calculates the Solar Homes hot water rebate on the remaining out-of-pocket price after STCs and VEECs are deducted. See the combined examples on /victoria/gas-hot-water-to-heat-pump/. Does replacing a bottled LPG water heater qualify for a VEU discount? Part 3 of the Victorian Energy Upgrades Specifications covers gas or LPG water heaters when replaced with an eligible heat pump or solar-boosted system in a building at least two years old. Because Energy Victoria's consumer table publishes only a mains gas figure, your accredited provider confirms the exact discount for an LPG replacement. Will a heat pump hot water system still work in a cold Victorian winter? Modern air-source heat pumps extract heat from outdoor air even in winter, though colder Victorian postcodes should choose a frost-protected model suited to cold climates (including models with a booster element where needed) and place the unit in a well-ventilated outdoor spot away from bedroom windows. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Gas Room Heater to Split System VEU Rebate Victoria Gas Room Heater to Split System VEU Rebate Victoria Replacing a non-ducted gas wall or room heater with an approved 3 to 9 kW reverse-cycle split system is the most common single-room VEU heating upgrade in Victoria. Energy Victoria publishes an indicative discount range because the exact amount depends on your new split system's capacity, efficiency rating, and postcode climate zone, and you must pay at least the minimum customer co-payment. Always involve an accredited provider before removing the old gas heater. $630 to $1,610 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Indicative VEU discount and annual bill savings According to Energy Victoria’s household heating and cooling page ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ): Replacing a non-ducted (room) gas heater with a 3 to 9 kW split system: $630 to $1,610 [source] . Estimated annual energy bill saving: up to $460 [source] per year. Installing a room split system without decommissioning an existing heater: $70 to $140 [source] . Minimum customer co-payment (single non-ducted split below 10 kW): at least $200 (including GST) [source] under VEU Specifications version 25.0 ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ). Single-room split system VEU discounts (with vs without decommissioning) · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 against Heating and cooling discounts — Victorian Energy Upgrades (Energy Victoria (DEECA)) ↗ . Indicative. The accredited provider confirms the final amount in your quote. Upgrade scenario Indicative VEU discount Replace a non-ducted (room) gas heater with a single split system (3 to 9 kW) $630 to $1,610 Install a room reverse-cycle split system without decommissioning an existing heater $70 to $140 Why the discount is a range and why decommissioning matters Energy Victoria shows $630 to $1,610 [source] as a range because certificate creation scales with the heating and cooling efficiency stars of the specific 3 to 9 kW model you pick, your VEU climate zone, and the accredited provider’s certificate pricing. To qualify for the gas-replacement range rather than the much smaller $70 to $140 [source] no-decommission discount: Your home must be more than 2 years old . A VEU accredited provider (or an installer working with one) must record pre-installation photos and details before the old gas wall furnace or space heater is disconnected—see our guide to the VEU timing and decommissioning rules . The old room gas heater must be safely decommissioned by a licensed gasfitter, and any wall or chimney opening sealed properly (see draught proofing discounts in Victoria ). Sizing your split system properly Energy Victoria’s buyers guide ( Energy Victoria — Reverse-cycle air conditioner buyers guide ) recommends asking for an in-home visit before choosing a unit: Avoid oversizing: A split system that is too large for the room cycles inefficiently and uses more electricity than needed. Compare heating capacity, cooling capacity, and noise: Check both winter heating output and outdoor condenser noise levels, especially near boundary fences or bedroom windows, and ensure at least a 5-year household warranty . Compare all room and ducted options on our Air Conditioner Rebate Victoria guide , check rules for Victorian renters , or run your scenario in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Why is the VEU discount for replacing a gas room heater shown as a range? The certificate count for a single split system replacing a non-ducted room gas heater varies with the heating and cooling efficiency rating and capacity of the new unit (from 3 kW to 9 kW), your postcode climate zone, and the accredited provider's current certificate pricing. See the published range in the table on /victoria/gas-room-heater-to-split-system/. Do I have to remove my old gas wall or room heater to get the higher VEU discount? Yes. To access the room gas heater replacement range, the existing fixed gas room heater must be formally decommissioned after pre-installation evidence is collected by an accredited provider in a home more than two years old. Installing a split system without decommissioning an existing heater receives a much smaller VEU discount. Why does Energy Victoria recommend a home visit before sizing a split system? Energy Victoria's buyers guide recommends having an installer inspect your room size, ceiling height, windows, and insulation first because a split system that is too large uses more energy than needed, while an undersized unit struggles in peak winter or summer. You should also compare outdoor unit noise ratings before choosing a placement. /victoria/gas-to-electric-hot-water-2027.text: Victoria 1 March 2027 Gas to Electric Hot Water Rule | Household Rebates Skip to main content Independent guide run by Agenor Services Pty Ltd (ABN 29 644 447 263). Not a government website. Installers may pay us for enquiries — how we're paid . Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Victoria 1 March 2027 Gas to Electric Hot Water Rule Victoria 1 March 2027 Gas to Electric Hot Water Rule From 1 March 2027, when a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing Victorian home needs replacing, it can no longer be replaced with another mains gas water heater and must be replaced with an electric system such as a heat pump or solar-boosted unit. Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program, replacing an inefficient gas hot water unit with an approved heat pump has a specific gas-replacement discount, and exemptions apply for certain technical constraints. $560 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 What changes on 1 March 2027 for existing Victorian homes Under Victoria’s electrification standards for buildings, from 1 March 2027 , an existing mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) that reaches the end of its service life and needs replacing cannot be replaced with another mains gas water heater. Instead, households must install an electric water heater—such as a heat pump or solar-boosted water heater—unless a regulatory exemption applies. Key boundaries confirmed by Energy Victoria and the Department of Transport and Planning: Working gas units do not need early removal: You only need to switch when your existing gas water heater breaks down and needs replacement. Repairs are still allowed: If your existing gas water heater can be safely repaired, you can repair it. Owner-occupier gas heating and cooking are not affected: Owner-occupiers are not required to remove or replace gas space heaters or gas cooktops. Bottled LPG is not affected: The Victoria Gas Substitution Roadmap confirms that homes using bottled LPG (rather than reticulated mains gas) are not affected by this rule. VEU discounts for switching from gas to electric hot water When replacing an inefficient mains gas hot water heater under the Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program, make sure you check the gas replacement row rather than the electric replacement row: Gas water heater to heat pump: indicative VEU discount of $560 [source] . Gas water heater to solar-boosted hot water: indicative discount of $700 [source] . Combined with Solar Homes hot water rebate: up to $1,560 [source] , or up to $1,960 [source] with an eligible locally made product (subject to a minimum customer co-contribution of $200 [source] ). Estimated annual bill savings: Energy Victoria estimates switching from gas to an efficient electric hot water system saves around $400 [source] per year. Exemptions in the regulation (reg 45E) The exemptions to the 1 March 2027 mains gas hot water replacement requirement are set out in the Plumbing Regulations, as amended by the Building and Plumbing Amendment Regulations 2025 ( Statutory Rule 140/2025 on legislation.vic.gov.au , full regulation text at AustLII reg 6 inserting reg 45E , alongside Victoria Government Gazette GG2025S654 ). Grouped as regulation 45E sets them out: Practical limits (45E(3)): not enough space inside, or no suitable outdoor space, for an electric water heater; a Class 2 building (apartments) or a pool served by a centralised gas system; an electric option would be unlawful under another law; installing an electric option would need the main switchboard or a distribution board altered; or it would need the electricity network augmented beyond a basic or standard connection. Kinds of work (45E(4)): temporary disconnection and reconnection; like-for-like replacement where the gas water heater does not need an electricity connection to run; or replacement within the warranty period. Timing (45E(5)): work under a contract signed before 1 March 2027, if done within 3 months after that date; building work under s10(1) or (2) of the Building Act carried out before 1 March 2027; or rectification orders issued before 1 March 2027. The rule applies to plumbers, and a plumber who breaches it faces a penalty of 20 penalty units. This is a plain-English summary, not legal advice. Your licensed plumber decides whether an exemption applies. See our dedicated guides on Victoria’s 2027 gas hot water exemptions and what happens if your gas hot water breaks before or after 1 March 2027 . Rules for rental properties from 1 March 2027 Rental properties face broader minimum efficiency standards from 1 March 2027 : Broken, unrepairable water heater: Must be replaced with an energy-efficient electric water heater (heat pump or electric-boosted solar). Broken, unrepairable main living area heater: Must be replaced with an energy-efficient reverse-cycle air conditioner. Start of a new lease: Efficient cooling must be installed in the main living area when a new lease starts from 1 March 2027. Frequently asked questions What happens on 1 March 2027 when a gas hot water system breaks down? From 1 March 2027, when a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing Victorian home reaches the end of its life and needs replacing, it generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas unit and must be replaced with an electric alternative such as a heat pump or solar-boosted system. Exemptions apply for certain technical constraints, and bottled LPG systems are not affected. Read the full details on /victoria/gas-to-electric-hot-water-2027/. Why is the VEU heat pump discount different when replacing gas versus electric hot water? Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades methodology, replacing an inefficient electric resistance water heater saves more calculated emissions than replacing a mains gas water heater, so the point-of-sale discount differs between the two scenarios. Check the exact figures for both replacement types on /victoria/heat-pump-rebate/. Are rental properties eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades discounts? Yes, rental properties in Victoria can access VEU discounts for approved reverse-cycle air conditioners and hot water upgrades, provided the building is more than two years old when replacing an existing system. Renters must have the landlord's approval before any heating, cooling, or hot water installation takes place. From 1 March 2027, new rental minimum efficiency standards also apply when systems fail or at the start of a new lease. Quote requests are not open yet We're not taking quote requests yet. To get a discount now, contact an accredited provider from Energy Victoria's list: Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts and providers ↗ Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts and providers ↗ Not sure which scenario applies to your home? Where these published running-cost estimates come from Rather than guessing your personal household consumption or assuming unverified retailer rates, this tool displays only Energy Victoria’s published Victorian household estimates : Gas to efficient electric hot water: Saves around $400 [source] per year ( Energy Victoria — Electric and efficiency standards for buildings ; Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ). See upfront discounts in gas hot water to heat pump and check tank volumes in our heat pump hot water size guide . Gas room heater to split-system reverse-cycle: Saves up to $460 [source] per year ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ). Ducted gas heater to ducted reverse-cycle: Saves up to $1,140 [source] per year ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ). Whole existing home going all-electric: Saves around $1,900 [source] per year without solar, or around $2,230 [source] per year with rooftop solar ( Energy Victoria — Electric and efficiency standards for buildings ), including about $350 to $400 [source] per year in avoided daily gas supply charges once your final gas appliance is disconnected ( Energy Victoria — Induction cooktop discounts ; see our Get-Off-Gas Planner ). Solar daytime timers and concession holders If your home has rooftop solar PV, running a heat pump water heater on a daytime timer lets you heat water with self-generated solar electricity instead of grid imports. Eligible cardholders should also check how the year-round Annual Electricity Concession compares with the six-month Winter Gas Concession on concession card holders in Victoria , and check upfront VEU discounts in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Check your household eligibility Run our Victoria Eligibility Checker to see which VEU discount scenarios and minimum co-payments fit your property. Open the Victoria Eligibility Checker Frequently asked questions Does switching gas heating or gas hot water save more each year in Victoria? Energy Victoria’s published estimates show larger annual savings from replacing whole-home ducted gas heating with ducted reverse-cycle air conditioning than from replacing a single room gas heater or gas hot water system alone. Upgrading hot water and heating together—and disconnecting your last gas appliance to stop daily supply charges—delivers the largest combined bill reduction; compare each published scenario in the picker above. How does rooftop solar affect annual electric running-cost savings? Energy Victoria publishes separate all-electric estimates for existing Victorian homes with and without rooftop solar PV, showing higher yearly savings when heat pumps and reverse-cycle air conditioners run during sunny daytime hours. Many heat pump water heaters include timers so water heating occurs when rooftop solar generation peaks. How do Victorian energy concessions affect switching from gas to electric? Eligible Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card, and DVA Gold Card holders receive the year-round Annual Electricity Concession on electricity usage and service charges above the annual threshold, whereas the Winter Gas Concession applies only from 1 May to 31 October. Read the full breakdown on /victoria/concession-card-holders/. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Geelong Air Conditioner & Heat Pump Rebates (VEU) Geelong Air Conditioner & Heat Pump Rebates (VEU) Households in Greater Geelong can claim upfront Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discounts when replacing older gas or electric heaters and hot water systems with approved reverse-cycle air conditioners or heat pumps. Detached Geelong homes replacing ducted gas heaters qualify for different VEU scenarios than single-room split upgrades. Always engage a VEU accredited provider (or an installer working with one) before any installation starts. $630 to $1,610 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Local context for Geelong (City of Greater Geelong) Postcodes covered on this page: 3215, 3216, 3218, 3220, 3221, 3226 City of Greater Geelong's Climate Change Response Plan supports residential electrification and replacing ageing gas heating across Geelong and the Bellarine. [City of Greater Geelong] Bureau of Meteorology climate records for Geelong show cooler winter overnight minimums (around 5.2°C to 5.6°C in July), making high-efficiency reverse-cycle heating and frost-protected heat pumps important. [Bureau of Meteorology (BoM)] Detached homes across Geelong suburbs like Belmont, Highton, and Grovedale with ducted gas heating can access VEU ducted or multi-split replacement scenarios if the home is over 2 years old. [Energy Victoria (DEECA)] Semi-rural properties around Greater Geelong on bottled LPG are not subject to the 1 March 2027 mains gas hot water replacement mandate, while reticulated mains gas homes are. [Department of Transport and Planning (Victoria)] In the VEU postcode table (VEU Specifications v25.0, Location Variable List), postcodes 3216, 3218 and 3220 are listed as Regional, with a Mild climatic region. Under Energy Victoria’s household heating and cooling scenarios: Replacing a room gas heater with a single split system (3–9 kW): indicative discount of $630 to $1,610 [source] . Replacing a ducted gas heater with a multi-split system: indicative discount of up to $2,940 [source] . Replacing a ducted gas heater with a 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system: indicative discount of up to $5,530 [source] (smaller 10 kW and 16 kW ducted systems have lower indicative amounts; see our Air Conditioner Rebate Victoria guide ). New growth-corridor estates in Armstrong Creek or Lara must check their occupancy date: if you are replacing an existing heater, the home must be more than 2 years old to qualify for a VEU replacement discount. Hot water upgrades in Geelong (mains gas vs electric vs LPG) For Geelong homes at least two years old replacing an existing hot water unit: Replacing an inefficient electric storage unit with a heat pump: indicative discount of $630 [source] . Replacing an inefficient mains gas unit with a heat pump: indicative discount of $560 [source] . Minimum customer co-contribution: $200 [source] . If your property is on reticulated mains gas, remember that from 1 March 2027 a mains gas water heater needing replacement must generally be replaced with an electric unit. Properties on outer Bellarine or rural fringes using bottled LPG are not affected by the 2027 mains gas replacement rule. Ceiling insulation discounts in Geelong Energy Victoria publishes two household ceiling insulation examples for an average 150 m² uninsulated or under-insulated home: up to $1,500 [source] in metro Melbourne (mild climate zone) and up to $2,100 [source] in regional Victoria (cold climate zone). Because postcodes 3216, 3218 and 3220 are listed in the VEU postcode table as Regional with a Mild climatic region, which example applies depends on how the program treats your postcode—the accredited provider confirms the amount in your quote. Read our full ceiling insulation rebate guide for safety checks and eligibility rules. Participating installers covering Geelong We do not yet have a signed partner installer covering Geelong postcodes. Until partner agreements for this area are finalised, you can search Energy Victoria's official accredited provider directory directly or check your upgrade scenario with our Victoria Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Why does the air conditioner discount vary so much between homes? The Victorian Energy Upgrades discount is calculated from the greenhouse gas savings of your specific upgrade. Replacing a whole-home ducted gas heater with a high-capacity ducted reverse-cycle system creates far more certificates than replacing a single room gas heater or installing a split system without decommissioning an existing heater. Compare the full scenario tables on /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/. Why is the VEU heat pump discount different when replacing gas versus electric hot water? Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades methodology, replacing an inefficient electric resistance water heater saves more calculated emissions than replacing a mains gas water heater, so the point-of-sale discount differs between the two scenarios. Check the exact figures for both replacement types on /victoria/heat-pump-rebate/. What happens on 1 March 2027 when a gas hot water system breaks down? From 1 March 2027, when a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing Victorian home reaches the end of its life and needs replacing, it generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas unit and must be replaced with an electric alternative such as a heat pump or solar-boosted system. Exemptions apply for certain technical constraints, and bottled LPG systems are not affected. Read the full details on /victoria/gas-to-electric-hot-water-2027/. Tick your gas appliances below to view Energy Victoria's indicative VEU discount for each step and the annual gas supply-charge saving once your final gas appliance is disconnected and your gas meter is abolished. $560 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Plan your gas-to-electric steps Tick the gas appliances in your home below to see each step’s indicative VEU discount, swap guide, and how abolishing your gas meter works once your last gas appliance is removed. See full rules: Gas room heater to split system guide . Ducted gas heater up to $5,530 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ The upper indicative figure applies specifically to replacing ducted gas with a large 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system; 10 kW, 16 kW, and multi-split options have separate figures. Gas cooktop $140 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ Existing homes do not have to remove gas cooktops; eligible 3-zone built-in or freestanding induction cooktops use a buy-first invoice claim process. See full rules: Gas cooktop to induction guide . Once your last gas appliance goes: supply-charge saving and abolishment about $350 to $400 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ Once every gas appliance at your property is disconnected, you can request permanent gas meter abolishment so daily gas supply charges stop: Request through your gas retailer: Contact your gas retailer (who coordinates with your local gas distributor). Example distributor timeframes (AusNet): AusNet lists 2 business days for gas meter removal and up to 15 business days for a permanent service cut-and-cap abolishment; Victoria’s other gas distributors may differ. Paperwork & timing: Read our step-by-step guide on how long a VEU upgrade and gas abolishment take , and check your distributor’s published tariff schedule for current abolishment charges. No single mandatory sequence—plan around appliance age and 2027 hot water rules Victorian building standards do not require existing owner-occupied homes to remove working gas space heaters or gas cooktops ( Energy Victoria — Existing residential buildings ). No official Victorian source prescribes a single order for going all-electric; instead, households usually weigh two practical triggers: The 1 March 2027 hot water trigger: When an existing mains gas water heater fails and needs replacing from 1 March 2027, it generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas heater (unless an exemption applies). Upfront VEU discounts per step: Replacing an inefficient mains gas water heater with a heat pump carries an indicative VEU discount of $560 [source] ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ); replacing a gas room heater with a split system lists $630 to $1,610 [source] , or replacing ducted gas with a large 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system lists up to $5,530 [source] ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ); and replacing a gas cooktop with an eligible induction cooktop lists $140 [source] per product ( Energy Victoria — Induction cooktop discounts ). Compare annual energy bill reductions across scenarios in our gas vs heat pump running costs picker . (Households in affected regional networks should also check extra assistance in Solstice gas shutdown towns .) How gas meter abolishment works once your last gas appliance goes Disconnecting your final gas appliance lets you close your gas account and avoid about $350 to $400 [source] per year in fixed gas supply charges ( Energy Victoria — Induction cooktop discounts ). Under Essential Services Commission rules, Victorian gas distributors must publish clear customer information on disconnection and permanent abolishment ( ESC — Gas Distribution System Code of Practice ). You request abolishment through your gas retailer : AusNet example timeframes: AusNet lists 2 business days for meter removal and up to 15 business days for a permanent service cut-and-cap ( AusNet — Requesting a gas disconnection, reconnection or abolishment ); other gas distributors (Australian Gas Networks and Multinet Gas Networks) may differ and publish their own regulated fee schedules. Timeline & compliance certificates: See how long a VEU upgrade and gas abolishment take , and check your current appliances in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Check your household eligibility Run our Victoria Eligibility Checker to see which VEU discount scenarios and minimum co-payments fit your property. Open the Victoria Eligibility Checker Frequently asked questions Is there an official order for replacing gas appliances in Victoria? No official Victorian Government source prescribes a mandatory sequence for electrifying an existing home, and owner-occupiers are not required to remove working gas space heaters or gas cooktops. The one legal trigger to plan around is 1 March 2027, when a mains gas water heater in an existing home that fails and needs replacement generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas unit. How do I abolish my gas meter once my last gas appliance is removed? Once a licensed gasfitter has disconnected and capped your final gas appliance, contact your gas retailer to request either meter removal or permanent service abolishment (cut-and-cap), which stops daily gas supply charges. AusNet publishes indicative timeframes of two business days for meter removal and up to 15 business days for service cut-and-cap, while other Victorian gas distributors publish their own schedules and regulated abolishment charges. Can I claim a separate VEU discount on each gas-to-electric step? Yes. Victorian Energy Upgrades offers separate household discounts across hot water, space heating and cooling, and induction cooktops, so you can electrify one appliance at a time or coordinate multiple upgrades without losing eligibility across categories. Remember to engage a VEU accredited provider before starting hot water or heating installation work. Households with frequent or simultaneous showers, baths, standard showerheads, or daytime solar timers often need to step up a tank size, while federal Small-scale Technology Certificates (STCs) apply only to air-source heat pumps under 425 litres. STC cap: Federal Small-scale Technology Certificates (STCs) apply only to air-source heat pumps with a volumetric capacity under 425 L ( Clean Energy Regulator (CER) ↗ ). How Energy Victoria’s tank sizing guide works Unlike instantaneous gas wall heaters that heat water on demand, a heat pump water heater stores heated water in an insulated tank. Energy Victoria’s consumer factsheet ( Energy Victoria — VEU water heating consumer factsheet (PDF) ) matches storage capacity to bedrooms first, then advises sizing up for heavy hot water routines or daytime-only solar timers. Compare upfront VEU and Solar Homes discounts depending on what you are replacing: Replacing a mains gas or LPG water heater with a heat pump Replacing an electric resistance water heater with a heat pump Heat Pump Hot Water Rebate Victoria overview Cold climates, noise, and the 425-litre STC threshold Before finalising a model with your plumber or VEU accredited provider: Cooler climates and frost protection: In cooler Victorian regions (such as Ballarat and other zone 5 postcodes), Energy Victoria advises considering a system with frost protection ( Energy Victoria — Existing residential buildings ), and the consumer factsheet notes electric booster elements can assist cold-weather recovery. Operating noise and placement: Energy Victoria’s factsheet notes that heat pumps produce noise comparable to an air conditioner while heating water, so position the tank and compressor clear of bedroom windows and neighbour fences. Under 425 L for federal STCs: Under Clean Energy Regulator rules, Small-scale Technology Certificates apply to eligible air-source heat pumps with a volumetric capacity under 425 L ( Clean Energy Regulator — Solar water heaters and air source heat pumps ). Energy Victoria’s water heating consumer factsheet notes that setting a timer to heat water mainly during daytime solar hours can require a slightly larger storage tank so your household has enough stored hot water overnight and the next morning. Discuss your household’s morning and evening shower routine with your plumber before choosing a tank capacity. What should households in cooler Victorian regions check when sizing a heat pump? In cooler climates—such as Victorian postcodes in VEU heat pump climatic zone 5—Energy Victoria advises considering a heat pump model with frost protection, and the consumer factsheet notes electric booster elements can help maintain recovery in cold conditions. Enter your postcode in the lookup above to check whether your area sits in zone 4 or zone 5. How noisy is a heat pump hot water system and where should it sit? Energy Victoria’s water heating consumer factsheet states that air-source heat pumps produce operating noise comparable to an outdoor air-conditioner compressor while actively heating water. Ask your plumber to position the unit in a well-ventilated outdoor spot away from bedroom windows and neighbour boundary fences. Notice that replacing an electric hot water unit carries a different VEU discount than replacing a mains gas unit. All household hot water upgrades require a building at least two years old, a minimum five-year product warranty, and a minimum customer contribution. $630 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Electric vs gas replacement: why the two figures differ A common misconception on rebate websites is quoting $630 [source] for every heat pump hot water upgrade. On Energy Victoria’s hot water discounts page, the indicative VEU discount depends on the fuel source of the system you are replacing: Replacing an inefficient electric water heater with a heat pump: indicative discount of $630 [source] (see our electric hot water to heat pump guide ). Replacing an inefficient gas water heater with a heat pump: indicative discount of $560 [source] (see our gas hot water to heat pump swap guide ). Replacing an inefficient electric water heater with a solar-boosted system: indicative discount of $910 [source] (see our solar hot water rebate guide ). Replacing an inefficient gas water heater with a solar-boosted system: indicative discount of $700 [source] . According to Energy Victoria, switching from a gas water heater to an efficient electric hot water system also saves households around $400 [source] per year on energy bills. To be eligible for the Solar Homes hot water rebate: You must be an owner-occupier of the home. Combined household taxable income must be under $150,000 [source] (from 1 July 2026; it was $210,000 [source] — see Solar Victoria's May 2026 announcement ). The property must be valued under $3 million [source] . The existing hot water system being replaced must be at least 3 years old from the date of purchase. You apply for pre-approval first , then have your system installed within 120 days . Household eligibility rules and the minimum contribution To be eligible for a VEU hot water discount in Victoria: Replacing an existing unit: You must be replacing an existing hot water system in a building that is at least 2 years old . New builds and properties without an existing water heater are not eligible. Maximum of two systems per household: Households can upgrade up to 2 hot water systems at the same address under the VEU program. Approved product and warranty: The new heat pump or solar-boosted unit must be on the VEU Register of Products and include a minimum 5-year warranty . Minimum customer contribution: Under VEU program rules, customers must pay a minimum co-contribution of $200 [source] toward the upgrade. Planning ahead for 1 March 2027 From 1 March 2027, mains gas water heaters that reach the end of their life in existing Victorian homes generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas unit. See our 1 March 2027 gas hot water rule guide for how this affects homeowners and landlords. Frequently asked questions Why is the VEU heat pump discount different when replacing gas versus electric hot water? Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades methodology, replacing an inefficient electric resistance water heater saves more calculated emissions than replacing a mains gas water heater, so the point-of-sale discount differs between the two scenarios. Check the exact figures for both replacement types on /victoria/heat-pump-rebate/. What happens on 1 March 2027 when a gas hot water system breaks down? From 1 March 2027, when a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing Victorian home reaches the end of its life and needs replacing, it generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas unit and must be replaced with an electric alternative such as a heat pump or solar-boosted system. Exemptions apply for certain technical constraints, and bottled LPG systems are not affected. Read the full details on /victoria/gas-to-electric-hot-water-2027/. Can I claim a Victorian Energy Upgrades discount after my system is already installed? Generally no. Energy Victoria advises that you must contact an accredited provider (or use an installer working with one) before buying or installing your system. Retrospective discounts after installation work has started are typically not possible. See our guide on /victoria/reverse-cycle-vs-gas-heater/ for how the timing rule works. Are rental properties eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades discounts? Yes, rental properties in Victoria can access VEU discounts for approved reverse-cycle air conditioners and hot water upgrades, provided the building is more than two years old when replacing an existing system. Renters must have the landlord's approval before any heating, cooling, or hot water installation takes place. From 1 March 2027, new rental minimum efficiency standards also apply when systems fail or at the start of a new lease. Quote requests are not open yet We're not taking quote requests yet. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria How Long Does a VEU Hot Water or Heating Upgrade Take? How Long Does a VEU Hot Water or Heating Upgrade Take? A Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) hot water or heating upgrade moves through quote verification, optional Solar Homes pre-approval, licensed installation, and post-installation compliance paperwork. If you are stacking the Solar Homes hot water rebate, you must receive pre-approval before work starts and complete installation within 120 days, and your plumber must issue a compliance certificate within five days of finishing eligible work. If you also abolish your mains gas connection afterwards, AusNet lists two business days for meter removal or up to 15 business days for a service cut-and-cap, though other gas distributors may differ. more than $750 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Building and Plumbing Commission (VBA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Steps from quote to compliance paperwork on a VEU upgrade Confirm approved models and quote with an accredited provider. Contact a VEU accredited provider or participating installer before touching your existing system so they can verify product eligibility and put the upfront VEU discount in writing. Obtain Solar Homes pre-approval if stacking on hot water. If you are an eligible owner-occupier combining Solar Homes with VEU on a hot water upgrade, wait for Solar Victoria pre-approval first—you then have 120 days to complete installation. Complete licensed installation and pre-removal evidence. Have the licensed plumber or electrician capture required pre-installation photos, install the approved system, and decommission the old unit safely. Receive your compliance certificate and optional gas abolishment. Collect your plumbing compliance certificate within five days of completion, let the accredited provider lodge VEU paperwork, and request gas disconnection through your energy retailer if leaving gas completely. Pre-approval and quoting milestones before installation Energy Victoria does not publish an official on-site installation duration because every switchboard, pipe run, and roof space differs—your installer will confirm their on-site schedule when quoting ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ; see how VEU quotes work ). Two official program rules govern the lead-up to installation day: VEU provider engagement first: The accredited provider confirms eligible models on the VEU Register of Products, quotes with the point-of-sale discount included, and handles the certificate paperwork ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ). Compare household setups in our gas hot water to heat pump guide . Solar Homes 120-day window: When stacking the Solar Homes hot water rebate, you must secure Solar Victoria pre-approval before installation begins (except under Solar Victoria’s emergency replacement pathway) and finish the installation within 120 days of pre-approval ( Solar Victoria — Hot water rebate ). If your tank has already failed, see what to do when a gas hot water unit breaks . Plumbing compliance certificates: the 5-day rule Under Victorian plumbing regulations, a licensed plumber must issue a plumbing compliance certificate within 5 days of completion whenever plumbing work is valued at more than $750 [source] or involves any Type A gas appliance work ( Victorian Building Authority — Plumbing compliance certificates ). Keep that compliance certificate alongside your tax invoice and electrical certificate of electrical safety—both your warranty and your provider’s VEU certificate creation depend on them. Gas meter removal and abolishment timeframes If your hot water or heating upgrade removes your last mains gas appliance and you decide to close your gas account ( see our Get-Off-Gas Planner ), you request disconnection or permanent abolishment through your gas retailer. On AusNet’s gas network, AusNet publishes indicative timeframes of 2 business days for a gas meter removal and up to 15 business days for a permanent service cut-and-cap abolishment ( AusNet — Requesting a gas disconnection, reconnection or abolishment ). Note: those timeframes are AusNet’s; Victoria’s other gas distributors (Australian Gas Networks and Multinet Gas Networks) may differ. Check your appliance path first in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions How soon after installation must my plumber issue a plumbing compliance certificate? According to the Building and Plumbing Commission, a licensed plumber must issue a plumbing compliance certificate within five days of completing any Type A gas appliance work or plumbing work above the statutory value threshold. How long does Solar Homes hot water pre-approval stay valid? Under Solar Victoria's hot water rebate rules, once your pre-approval application is accepted you have 120 days to have your eligible system installed and submitted. How long does gas meter removal or service abolishment take once I leave mains gas? Timeframes vary by gas distributor and are arranged through your gas retailer: on AusNet's network, meter removal takes around two business days while full service cut-and-cap abolishment takes up to 15 business days. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Victorian Landlord 2027 Rental Energy Efficiency Standards Victorian Landlord 2027 Rental Energy Efficiency Standards Under Victoria's new minimum rental energy efficiency standards, rental providers face staged compliance triggers starting 1 March 2027 across ceiling insulation, showerheads, cooling, hot water, heating, and (from 1 July 2027) draught proofing. Consumer Affairs Victoria confirms that every standard's required upgrade is eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discounts through accredited providers, and rental providers can also access Solar Homes solar PV rebates on up to two rentals per financial year. This guide is a plain-English summary, not legal advice—check Consumer Affairs Victoria for binding rules and exemptions. $630 to $1,610 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Timeline of Victorian rental minimum standards (2027–2030) This page is a plain-English summary for rental providers and property managers, not legal advice —refer to Consumer Affairs Victoria for full regulatory obligations ( Consumer Affairs Victoria — New minimum energy efficiency standards ; Energy Victoria — Energy efficiency for rental properties ). Rental standard Compliance trigger and start date Minimum technical specification Ceiling insulation New lease from 1 March 2027 (where no ceiling insulation is present) At least R5.0 ceiling insulation ( ceiling insulation guide ) Showerheads New lease from 1 March 2027 4-star WELS water-efficiency rating Hot water From 1 March 2027 , when an existing water heater fails beyond repair Energy-efficient electric: heat pump or electric-boosted solar ( gas-to-heat-pump guide ) Main living area heating From 1 March 2027 , when the existing fixed heater fails beyond repair Reverse-cycle air conditioner: 2-star+ GEMS heating rating (non-ducted) or HSPF ≥ 3.2 (ducted) for the climate area Main living area cooling New lease from 1 March 2027 ; all rentals from 1 July 2030 Fixed cooling: 3-star+ GEMS cooling rating (non-ducted) or TCSPF ≥ 3.8 (ducted) Draught proofing New lease from 1 July 2027 Weather sealing external doors, windows, and unused chimneys/vents VEU and Solar Homes discounts rental providers can claim Consumer Affairs Victoria confirms that upgrades installed to meet these minimum rental standards are eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discounts ( Consumer Affairs Victoria — Minimum energy efficiency standards ). Energy Victoria’s rental properties guide highlights the following indicative incentives ( Energy Victoria — Energy efficiency for rental properties ): Room gas heater to split-system reverse-cycle air conditioner: $630 to $1,610 [source] . Ducted gas heater to a large 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle system: up to $5,530 [source] (note that this upper figure applies specifically to a 22.4 kW ducted replacement; smaller 10 kW and 16 kW ducted systems receive smaller discounts—see all ducted sizes ). Inefficient gas water heater to a heat pump: $560 [source] . Solar Homes rooftop solar PV for rentals: up to $1,400 [source] on up to 2 rental properties per financial year (subject to Solar Victoria’s rental provider eligibility rules). See how tenants and landlords coordinate upgrades on our Victorian renters guide . Summary of exemptions (check CAV for details) Consumer Affairs Victoria outlines exemptions where installing a standard upgrade is impractical or unlawful ( Consumer Affairs Victoria — Minimum energy efficiency standards ), including: Properties served by centralised heating, cooling, or hot water systems (such as many multi-storey apartment buildings). Buildings with no suitable outdoor space to mount a heat pump or air-conditioner compressor. Heritage overlays or owners-corporation rules that prohibit the external installation. Always check Consumer Affairs Victoria’s official guidance for the documentation required to rely on an exemption, and run your rental property’s existing appliances through the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions When does each Victorian rental energy efficiency standard start? From 1 March 2027, ceiling insulation to at least R5.0 (where none is present), 4-star WELS showerheads, and main living area cooling apply at the start of a new lease, while failed hot water units and failed main living area heaters must be replaced with efficient electric systems when they break down beyond repair. Draught-proofing standards commence on 1 July 2027, and the cooling requirement applies across all remaining rentals from 1 July 2030. Can Victorian rental providers claim VEU discounts and Solar Homes rebates? Yes. Consumer Affairs Victoria notes that upgrades meeting the rental minimum standards are eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades point-of-sale discounts through accredited providers, including reverse-cycle air conditioning, heat pump hot water, ceiling insulation, and weather sealing. Energy Victoria also notes that rental providers can apply for the Solar Homes solar panel rebate on up to two rental properties per financial year; see the indicative amounts in the sections above. What exemptions apply to Victoria’s 2027 rental minimum energy efficiency standards? Consumer Affairs Victoria lists specific technical and legal exemptions, including buildings served by centralised heating, cooling, or hot water systems, properties with no suitable space for an external compressor, heritage restrictions, or owners-corporation rules that prohibit the installation. Because exemptions depend on your building and lease circumstances, check Consumer Affairs Victoria’s official guidance before relying on an exemption. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Melbourne Air Conditioner & Heat Pump Rebates (VEU) Melbourne Air Conditioner & Heat Pump Rebates (VEU) Households across Greater Melbourne can access Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) upfront discounts when replacing gas or electric heating and hot water systems with approved reverse-cycle air conditioners or heat pumps. Because certificate values incorporate regional climate zones, metropolitan Melbourne upgrades follow Victoria's metropolitan schedule. Make sure a VEU accredited provider is engaged before any installation or decommissioning starts. $630 to $1,610 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Local context for Melbourne (City of Melbourne, City of Yarra, City of Merri-bek, City of Boroondara, City of Port Phillip) Postcodes covered on this page: 3000, 3004, 3051, 3056, 3121, 3182 City of Melbourne's Zero Carbon Buildings program supports apartment owners corporations and households transitioning off reticulated gas. [City of Melbourne] Bureau of Meteorology winter averages for Melbourne show July mean minimum temperatures around 7.1°C, driving substantial winter space-heating demand. [Bureau of Meteorology (BoM)] Older inner-Melbourne terraces and apartments replacing room gas heaters or electric storage water heaters must meet the 2-year building age rule under VEU. [Energy Victoria (DEECA)] From 1 March 2027, Melbourne rental properties must meet Victorian minimum efficiency standards for hot water and main living area heating and cooling.
