Whole-home ducted reverse-cycle replacing ducted gas heating: indicative discount of up to $5,530 [source] for the largest 22.4 kW ducted systems (smaller capacities receive lower discounts; see the full table on our Air Conditioner Rebate Victoria guide ). For strata apartments and townhouses in the City of Melbourne and surrounding councils, remember that outdoor condenser placement and body corporate rules should be checked before installation, and your installer must record pre-installation photos of any decommissioned heater before work starts. Heat pump hot water discounts in Melbourne When replacing an existing hot water unit in a Melbourne building at least two years old: Inefficient electric water heater to heat pump: indicative VEU discount of $630 [source] . Inefficient mains gas water heater to heat pump: indicative VEU discount of $560 [source] . Every VEU hot water upgrade requires a minimum customer co-contribution of $200 [source] . From 1 March 2027 , a mains gas water heater in an existing Melbourne home that needs replacement must generally be replaced with an efficient electric unit unless an exemption (such as a major switchboard alteration or certain apartment constraints) applies. Participating installers covering Melbourne We do not yet have a signed partner installer covering Melbourne postcodes. Until partner agreements for this area are finalised, you can search Energy Victoria's official accredited provider directory directly or check your upgrade scenario with our Victoria Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Why does the air conditioner discount vary so much between homes? The Victorian Energy Upgrades discount is calculated from the greenhouse gas savings of your specific upgrade. Replacing a whole-home ducted gas heater with a high-capacity ducted reverse-cycle system creates far more certificates than replacing a single room gas heater or installing a split system without decommissioning an existing heater. Compare the full scenario tables on /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/. What happens on 1 March 2027 when a gas hot water system breaks down? From 1 March 2027, when a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing Victorian home reaches the end of its life and needs replacing, it generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas unit and must be replaced with an electric alternative such as a heat pump or solar-boosted system. Exemptions apply for certain technical constraints, and bottled LPG systems are not affected. Read the full details on /victoria/gas-to-electric-hot-water-2027/. Are rental properties eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades discounts? Yes, rental properties in Victoria can access VEU discounts for approved reverse-cycle air conditioners and hot water upgrades, provided the building is more than two years old when replacing an existing system. Renters must have the landlord's approval before any heating, cooling, or hot water installation takes place. From 1 March 2027, new rental minimum efficiency standards also apply when systems fail or at the start of a new lease. Quote requests are not open yet We're not taking quote requests yet. Because some Peninsula towns use reticulated mains gas while hinterland and coastal pockets rely on electric storage or bottled LPG, your exact VEU discount depends on your current system. Always involve an accredited provider before work begins. $630 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Local context for Mornington Peninsula (Mornington Peninsula Shire) Postcodes covered on this page: 3930, 3931, 3934, 3936, 3939, 3941, 3943 Mornington Peninsula Shire's Climate Emergency Plan supports residential energy efficiency and electrifying household heating and hot water across Peninsula townships. [Bureau of Meteorology (BoM)] While Mornington, Mount Eliza, Dromana, and Rosebud have reticulated mains gas, many properties in Red Hill, Main Ridge, Flinders, and Cape Schanck use electric storage or bottled LPG. Reverse-cycle air conditioning discounts on the Peninsula Whether you are upgrading a permanent family home or a holiday property (provided it is a residential home more than 2 years old when replacing an existing heater): Replacing a room gas heater with a split system (3–9 kW): indicative discount of $630 to $1,610 [source] . Replacing a hard-wired electric room heater (such as wall panel heaters) with a split system: indicative discount of up to $840 [source] . Frequently asked questions Why is the VEU heat pump discount different when replacing gas versus electric hot water? Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades methodology, replacing an inefficient electric resistance water heater saves more calculated emissions than replacing a mains gas water heater, so the point-of-sale discount differs between the two scenarios. Check the exact figures for both replacement types on /victoria/heat-pump-rebate/. What happens on 1 March 2027 when a gas hot water system breaks down? From 1 March 2027, when a mains gas water heater (including a gas pool heater) in an existing Victorian home reaches the end of its life and needs replacing, it generally cannot be replaced with another mains gas unit and must be replaced with an electric alternative such as a heat pump or solar-boosted system. Exemptions apply for certain technical constraints, and bottled LPG systems are not affected. Read the full details on /victoria/gas-to-electric-hot-water-2027/. Can I claim a Victorian Energy Upgrades discount after my system is already installed? Generally no. Energy Victoria advises that you must contact an accredited provider (or use an installer working with one) before buying or installing your system. Retrospective discounts after installation work has started are typically not possible. See our guide on /victoria/reverse-cycle-vs-gas-heater/ for how the timing rule works. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria New Homes All-Electric Victoria 2027: Rules & Rebates New Homes All-Electric Victoria 2027: Rules & Rebates From 1 January 2027, new homes and most new commercial buildings in Victoria—including knock-down rebuilds—must be built all-electric when the building permit is issued on or after 1 January 2027, and existing buildings without gas can no longer connect to mains gas. Because most Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) replacement discounts require a building more than two years old, brand-new homes receive smaller no-decommissioning VEU air-conditioning discounts instead, alongside Solar Homes solar panel rebates during construction. $70 to $140 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Victoria’s 1 January 2027 all-electric standard for new builds Under Victoria’s building electrification rules ( Energy Victoria — New buildings (residential and most commercial) ): New homes and knock-down rebuilds: Must be all-electric where the building permit is issued on or after 1 January 2027 (also covering most new commercial buildings), subject to a limited transitional exception where substantial design progress has been certified. Existing buildings without mains gas: Cannot connect to the reticulated gas network from 1 January 2027 . (For homes that already have mains gas, see how the separate March 2027 hot water rule works in our 2027 gas-to-electric hot water guide .) Estimated annual bill savings: Energy Victoria estimates that a new all-electric home saves $990 [source] a year on energy bills compared with a dual-fuel home, rising to $1,920 [source] a year when paired with rooftop solar ( Energy Victoria — New buildings ). Why homes under 2 years old miss most VEU replacement discounts Homeowners in fast-growing outer-suburban estates (such as Wyndham , Casey, and Whittlesea) often wonder why a 1-year-old house cannot claim the large heating or hot water VEU discounts: The 2-year building-age rule: VEU household replacement discounts for heating/cooling and hot water require your home to be more than 2 years old ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ; Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ). Small VEU discount with no heater decommissioned: For a new build installing a reverse-cycle air conditioner where no old heater is removed, Energy Victoria lists a typical VEU discount of $70 to $140 [source] ( Energy Victoria — New buildings ; see Air Conditioner Rebate Victoria ). Solar Homes rebate for homes under construction Eligible owner-occupiers building an all-electric home can apply for the Solar Homes solar panel (PV) rebate of up to $1,400 [source] (plus an optional matching interest-free loan) while the home is under construction , with 270 days from approval to complete the solar installation ( Energy Victoria — New buildings ; Solar Victoria — Solar panel rebate ). Compare income and property value caps in VEU vs Solar Homes , or check your home’s age and appliances in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Does my building permit date decide whether Victoria’s 2027 all-electric new-home rule applies? Yes. Energy Victoria states that the all-electric standard for new homes and knock-down rebuilds applies to building permits issued on or after 1 January 2027, with a limited transitional exception where substantial design progress is certified under the regulations. Existing buildings without an existing gas connection also cannot connect to mains gas from 1 January 2027. Why can’t newly built homes get the larger VEU heating and hot water replacement discounts? Most higher-value VEU household heating, cooling, and hot water discounts require decommissioning an existing inefficient system in a home that is more than two years old. Newly constructed homes have no old system to decommission and are under two years old, though Energy Victoria notes a modest VEU discount still exists when installing a reverse-cycle air conditioner with no heater decommissioned. Can I claim the Solar Homes solar panel rebate while my new home is under construction? Yes. Energy Victoria and Solar Victoria allow eligible owner-occupiers building a new home to apply for the Solar Homes solar panel (PV) rebate while the home is under construction, with up to 270 days from approval to complete the solar installation. Not a government website. Installers may pay us for enquiries — how we're paid . Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Can Renters Get VEU Discounts in Victoria? (2026–27 Guide) Can Renters Get VEU Discounts in Victoria? (2026–27 Guide) Victorian renters are eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discounts across private rental homes, though you should check with your rental provider first because landlord permission is required for appliance or fixture upgrades. Renters can make minor changes—such as LED globes requiring no new fittings, low-flow showerheads if you keep the original, and non-permanent window film—without asking first, and draught proofing is a reasonable change a landlord cannot refuse without good reason. From 1 March 2027, new minimum rental energy efficiency standards also require landlords to upgrade insulation, hot water, heating, cooling, and draught proofing on set triggers. By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 How VEU works for renters and private rentals Private rental properties across Victoria can access Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) discounts on heating and cooling, hot water, ceiling insulation, and weather sealing when tenants and rental providers work together ( Energy Victoria — Renters, landlords and body corporate ; Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ). Check with your rental provider first: Because replacing a fixed heater (such as swapping a gas room heater for a split system ), changing a hot water unit, or adding ceiling insulation alters the property, written permission from your landlord is needed before any VEU accredited provider starts work. Note on Solar Homes hot water: Unlike VEU, Solar Victoria’s Solar Homes hot water rebate is generally restricted to owner-occupiers ( Solar Victoria — Hot water rebate ), with a specific exception for affected properties in Solstice Energy gas shutdown towns ( Solar Victoria — Supporting Solstice customers ). Bill concessions still apply directly to renters: If you hold an eligible concession card and your name is on the electricity or gas account, see our guide for concession card holders in Victoria . Changes renters can make without or with reasonable-change rules Consumer Affairs Victoria sets out clear rules on energy-saving changes in rented homes ( Consumer Affairs Victoria — Renters making changes to the property ): No permission required: Installing LED light bulbs that do not need new light fittings, fitting a low-flow showerhead (provided you store the original showerhead and refit it when moving out), and applying removable non-permanent window film. Draught proofing (“reasonable change”): In a rental property without gas appliances, draught proofing ( see VEU weather sealing ) is classed as a reasonable change that a rental provider cannot refuse without a good reason . In a property with gas appliances, a gas safety check is required first to prevent carbon monoxide hazards. What your landlord must upgrade from 2027 From 1 March 2027 , Victoria’s minimum rental energy efficiency standards begin phasing in across ceiling insulation, 4-star WELS showerheads, main living area cooling, and end-of-life replacements of failed hot water and main living area heaters, followed by draught proofing from 1 July 2027 ( Consumer Affairs Victoria — New minimum energy efficiency standards ). Share our full 2027 Victorian landlord standards and VEU discount guide with your rental provider or property manager, or check upgrade scenarios in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Do Victorian renters need their landlord’s permission for a VEU upgrade? Renters are eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades discounts, and Energy Victoria advises checking with your rental provider first because written permission is required for fixture or appliance changes. Private rental properties can access VEU heating, cooling, hot water, and insulation discounts when tenants and landlords coordinate before work starts. Under Consumer Affairs Victoria rules, draught proofing is treated as a reasonable change a rental provider cannot refuse without good reason in a home with no gas appliances, while properties with gas appliances need a gas safety check first. What energy-saving changes can a Victorian renter make without landlord permission? Consumer Affairs Victoria states that renters can install energy-efficient LED light globes that need no new light fittings, low-flow showerheads provided they keep and reinstall the original showerhead later, and non-permanent window film without asking permission first. Any hard-wired heating, cooling, hot water, or ceiling insulation upgrade requires working with your rental provider before booking an accredited provider. What must Victorian rental providers upgrade from 1 March 2027? From 1 March 2027, Victorian minimum rental energy efficiency standards introduce requirements for ceiling insulation and 4-star WELS showerheads at a new lease, main living area cooling at a new lease, and efficient electric replacements when an existing hot water unit or main living area heater fails beyond repair. Draught-proofing requirements start from 1 July 2027, and cooling extends to all rentals from 1 July 2030, subject to narrow exemptions. Read the full timeline on /victoria/landlords-rental-standards-2027/. /victoria/reverse-cycle-vs-gas-heater/.text: Reverse-Cycle vs Gas Heater: The VEU Timing Rule | Household Rebates Skip to main content Independent guide run by Agenor Services Pty Ltd (ABN 29 644 447 263). Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria Reverse-Cycle vs Gas Heater: The VEU Timing Rule Reverse-Cycle vs Gas Heater: The VEU Timing Rule Under Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) rules, you must engage an accredited provider (or an installer working with one) before any installation or heater decommissioning work starts. Retrospective discounts after a system has already been installed are typically not possible. Furthermore, the size of your reverse-cycle air conditioning discount depends heavily on whether an existing gas or electric heater is formally decommissioned as part of the upgrade. $630 to $1,610 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Why “provider before work starts” is the golden rule of VEU Energy Victoria states clearly on its product and program pages that households should contact an accredited provider before purchasing or installing any product, and that retrospective discounts are typically not possible . If you hire your own electrician or plumber, that tradesperson must already work with a VEU accredited provider before any work starts . Why does timing matter so much? Because the accredited provider must collect specific geo-tagged photographs, serial numbers, and compliance declarations before the existing gas or electric heater is disconnected and removed. Once an old heater is on the nature strip or taken away without pre-installation evidence, the upgrade cannot be claimed as a heater replacement. Decommissioning vs installing without decommissioning The difference in VEU certificate value between decommissioning an existing gas heater and installing a new air conditioner without decommissioning an existing heater is substantial: Room split system (3–9 kW) replacing and decommissioning a room gas heater: indicative discount of $630 to $1,610 [source] (see our gas room heater to split-system swap guide ). Room split system installed without decommissioning an existing heater: indicative discount of $70 to $140 [source] . 22.4 kW ducted reverse-cycle replacing and decommissioning a ducted gas heater: indicative discount of up to $5,530 [source] . Ducted reverse-cycle installed without decommissioning an existing heater: indicative discount of up to $410 [source] . Keep in mind that from 30 September 2026 under VEU Specifications v25.0, any ducted reverse-cycle air conditioner also requires a minimum customer co-payment of at least $3,000 (including GST) [source] per installed product. See the full breakdown of co-payment tiers in our air conditioner rebate co-payment guide . In addition, when replacing an existing heater, the building must be more than 2 years old . Already bought a unit in a retail sale? Stop before installing If you have already purchased an approved reverse-cycle unit from a retailer but have not yet installed it, contact a VEU accredited provider before booking installation. Once installation work starts without a provider involved, a retrospective VEU discount is generally not possible. Running cost comparison: reverse-cycle vs gas heating Energy Victoria’s household guidance highlights that modern reverse-cycle air conditioners are significantly cheaper to run than mains gas heaters: Switching from a room gas heater to a split-system reverse-cycle unit saves up to $460 [source] a year on energy bills. Switching from a ducted gas heater to a ducted reverse-cycle system saves up to $1,140 [source] a year on energy bills. Rental minimum standards from 1 March 2027 For Victorian landlords and tenants: Renters can access VEU heating and cooling discounts today, provided they have the landlord’s approval before work starts. From 1 March 2027 , when a fixed heater in a rental home’s main living area breaks down and cannot be repaired, the landlord must replace it with an energy-efficient reverse-cycle air conditioner. From 1 March 2027 , rental properties must also have efficient cooling in the main living area at the start of a new lease. Frequently asked questions Can I claim a Victorian Energy Upgrades discount after my system is already installed? Generally no. Energy Victoria advises that you must contact an accredited provider (or use an installer working with one) before buying or installing your system. Retrospective discounts after installation work has started are typically not possible. See our guide on /victoria/reverse-cycle-vs-gas-heater/ for how the timing rule works. Why does the air conditioner discount vary so much between homes? The Victorian Energy Upgrades discount is calculated from the greenhouse gas savings of your specific upgrade. Replacing a whole-home ducted gas heater with a high-capacity ducted reverse-cycle system creates far more certificates than replacing a single room gas heater or installing a split system without decommissioning an existing heater. Compare the full scenario tables on /victoria/air-conditioner-rebate/. Are rental properties eligible for Victorian Energy Upgrades discounts? Yes, rental properties in Victoria can access VEU discounts for approved reverse-cycle air conditioners and hot water upgrades, provided the building is more than two years old when replacing an existing system. Renters must have the landlord's approval before any heating, cooling, or hot water installation takes place. From 1 March 2027, new rental minimum efficiency standards also apply when systems fail or at the start of a new lease. Under Victoria's 2027 rental energy efficiency standards, either a heat pump or an electric-boosted solar water heater satisfies the electric hot water requirement when an old unit fails. Engage an accredited provider before starting any replacement work. $910 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 VEU discounts for solar-boosted hot water systems Energy Victoria publishes two household VEU figures for installing an approved solar-boosted hot water system in a building at least two years old ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ): Replacing an inefficient electric water heater with a solar-boosted system: $910 [source] . Replacing an inefficient gas water heater with a solar-boosted system: $700 [source] . Household solar-boosted hot water VEU discounts · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 against Hot water system discounts — Victorian Energy Upgrades (Energy Victoria (DEECA)) ↗ . Indicative. The accredited provider confirms the final amount in your quote. Upgrade scenario Indicative VEU discount Replace an inefficient electric hot water system with a solar-boosted hot water system $910 Replace an inefficient gas hot water heater with a solar-boosted hot water system $700 If roof-mounted solar collectors do not suit your roof pitch, shading, or plumbing layout, compare air-source heat pump alternatives in our Heat Pump Rebate Victoria guide , electric hot water to heat pump guide , and gas hot water to heat pump guide . Replacing a broken solar hot water system If your existing rooftop solar water heater has failed, Energy Victoria explicitly lists broken, out-of-warranty solar hot water systems (whether electric-boosted or gas-boosted) among the systems eligible to be replaced with an approved heat pump or new solar-boosted system. Energy Victoria also notes that some older gas-boosted and electric-boosted solar heaters count as inefficient systems under the VEU schedule—your accredited provider checks your existing model’s eligibility before quoting. Electric-boosted vs gas-boosted solar and locally made products When choosing between electric-boosted and gas-boosted solar hot water: 2027 rental and building standards: Under Victoria’s rental energy efficiency standards from 1 March 2027 ( Energy Victoria — Energy efficiency for rental properties ), when an existing rental water heater breaks down and cannot be repaired, the rental provider must install an energy-efficient electric system—specifically a heat pump or an electric-boosted solar water heater (see Victorian landlord 2027 standards ). Solar Victoria locally made list: On Solar Victoria’s hot water rebate page ( Solar Victoria — Hot water rebate ), the list of products eligible for the locally made incentive includes selected Dux electric-boosted solar models (listed by Solar Victoria alongside locally made heat pumps; check Solar Victoria’s current product list rather than treating this as an endorsement). Compare VEU vs Solar Homes eligibility or test your home in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Can I get a VEU discount to replace a broken solar hot water system? Energy Victoria lists broken, out-of-warranty electric-boosted or gas-boosted solar water heaters among the systems that can be replaced with an approved heat pump or new solar-boosted water heater, and also notes that some older solar heaters count as inefficient systems. Your accredited provider checks your existing model before quoting. What is the difference between gas-boosted and electric-boosted solar hot water under Victoria's rules? An electric-boosted solar water heater uses an electric element for cloudy-day backup rather than mains gas, so it satisfies Victoria's 1 March 2027 rental and existing-home electric replacement standards, whereas new mains gas replacements are phased out from 1 March 2027 unless an exemption applies. Are any solar hot water models eligible for Solar Victoria's locally made incentive? Solar Victoria's locally made product list for the Solar Homes hot water rebate includes selected Dux electric-boosted solar models alongside Australian-made heat pumps. Always check Solar Victoria's current eligible product list before pre-approval. Not a government website. Installers may pay us for enquiries — how we're paid . Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria VEU Minimum Co-Payment Victoria: 2026 Rules by Upgrade VEU Minimum Co-Payment Victoria: 2026 Rules by Upgrade Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program, the point-of-sale certificate discount cannot reduce your out-of-pocket payment to zero—you must pay at least the mandatory minimum customer co-payment including GST. From 30 September 2026, higher household co-payments apply to larger split systems, multi-splits, and all ducted reverse-cycle air conditioners under VEU Specifications version 25. Any advertisement, cold call, or quote promising a zero-cost ducted air conditioner or offering to refund your co-payment cannot be a genuine VEU upgrade. $200 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Household minimum co-payments from 30 September 2026 Victorian Energy Upgrades Specifications 2018 Version 25.0 sets mandatory minimum customer co-payments (all including GST) across household heating and cooling, ceiling insulation, and induction cooktops ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ): Mandatory VEU household minimum co-payments (incl GST) · Checked on 13 Nov 2026 against Victorian Energy Upgrades Specifications 2018 Version 25.0 (PDF) (Department of Energy, Environment and Climate Action (DEECA)) ↗ . Indicative. The accredited provider confirms the final amount in your quote. Upgrade scenario Minimum customer co-payment Any ducted reverse-cycle air conditioner, per installed product (activities 6A–6C) (From 30 Sept 2026) at least $3,000 (including GST) Induction cooktop, per product at least $200 (including GST) Ceiling insulation (activity 48) at least $200 (including GST) Multi-split, total rated cooling capacity 10 kW or more (From 30 Sept 2026) at least $3,000 (including GST) Multi-split, total rated cooling capacity below 10 kW (From 30 Sept 2026) at least $1,000 (including GST) Other non-ducted system, 10 kW or more (From 30 Sept 2026) at least $1,000 (including GST) Other non-ducted (single split) system, below 10 kW (From 30 Sept 2026) at least $200 (including GST) Before 30 September 2026 , the minimum co-payment for a household ducted reverse-cycle air conditioner was at least $1,000 (including GST) [source] . From 30 September 2026 it is at least $3,000 (including GST) [source] per installed ducted product, and multi-split systems of 10 kW or more also carry a at least $3,000 (including GST) [source] minimum co-payment. Compare how this affects whole-home upgrades in our guides to replacing ducted gas with ducted reverse-cycle and replacing ducted gas with split systems or multi-split . Hot water and commercial minimum contributions For household hot water upgrades (VEU activities 1 and 3—electric-to-heat-pump and gas-to-heat-pump or solar water heaters), the minimum customer payment is $200 [source] per product including GST ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ; Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ). Energy Victoria also notes that larger commercial and industrial upgrades carry a at least $10,000 [source] minimum co-payment ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts )—that threshold applies only to large business projects, not residential homes. Why “zero-cost ducted” offers are a red flag Because VEEC discounts are deducted from the supplied-and-installed price subject to the mandatory co-payment floor: No genuine zero-cost ducted system: A legitimate VEU provider cannot legally supply and install a household ducted reverse-cycle air conditioner without collecting at least at least $3,000 (including GST) [source] including GST from the customer. No cashback or rebates of the co-payment: Accredited providers and installers are prohibited from reimbursing, rebating, or crediting back the mandatory minimum co-payment after installation. Report suspicious marketing: If a marketer contacts you uninvited or promises an upgrade with nothing to pay, read our guide to VEU scams, cold-call bans, and how to report non-compliance , and check genuine rules first with our Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Why can't a VEU discount cover the entire cost of my upgrade? Victorian Energy Upgrades rules set mandatory minimum customer co-payments across hot water, heating and cooling, ceiling insulation, and induction cooktops so households contribute toward the equipment and installation rather than receiving zero-cost installations. Check the full co-payment table on /victoria/veu-minimum-co-payment/. Can an installer refund or waive my VEU minimum co-payment? No. Under VEU Specifications version 25.0, the customer must genuinely pay at least the required GST-inclusive minimum co-payment per installed product, and an installer or accredited provider must not rebate, refund, or disguise that minimum contribution. How did the heating and cooling minimum co-payments change on 30 September 2026? From 30 September 2026 under VEU Specifications version 25.0 (Part 6), the mandatory minimum customer co-payment increased for all household ducted reverse-cycle systems and larger multi-split or non-ducted systems, while single non-ducted splits below 10 kW kept the lower tier. Compare every tier on /victoria/veu-minimum-co-payment/. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria VEU Scams, Cold Calls and Door-Knocking Bans in Victoria VEU Scams, Cold Calls and Door-Knocking Bans in Victoria Unsolicited telemarketing cold calls and door-to-door sales visits for Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) are banned across Victoria unless you gave express prior consent to be contacted. Marketers and installers must never claim to work for the Victorian Government, the VEU program, or the Essential Services Commission, and must explain that participating in VEU is completely voluntary. Household Rebates is not a government website and never cold-calls or doorknocks. By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Cold calls and doorknocking are banned under VEU Under Victorian Energy Upgrades consumer protection laws enforced by the Essential Services Commission ( ESC — Cold-call telemarketing and doorknocking bans ): Telemarketing cold calls have been banned since 1 May 2024 . Unsolicited doorknocking has been banned since 1 August 2024 . An accredited provider, installer, or marketer may only call or visit your home if you gave express prior consent first—see how VEU quotes and consent rules work . For clarity, Household Rebates is an independent information guide ( about us ), not a government website, and we never cold-call or doorknock . Red flags and what VEU marketers must tell you Under the VEU code of conduct ( ESC — Your consumer rights in the VEU program ), anyone marketing or quoting a VEU upgrade: Must not claim to work for the Victorian Energy Upgrades program, the Essential Services Commission, or the Victorian Government. Must not tell you that a VEU upgrade is compulsory or urgent government work—they must tell you that participation is voluntary . Must not advertise a zero-dollar household hot water, air-conditioning, insulation, or induction upgrade that ignores the mandatory VEU minimum co-payment . Before agreeing to any quote, you can verify accredited businesses yourself using our guide on how to find and check a VEU accredited provider or test your home’s setup in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . How complaints work and where to report breaches Accredited providers must acknowledge consumer complaints within 5 business days and aim to resolve them within 20 business days ( ESC — Your consumer rights in the VEU program ). If you receive an illegal cold call or doorknock, or cannot resolve an issue with a provider, contact the regulators listed on Energy Victoria and ESC pages ( Energy Victoria — Your rights ; ESC — Report non-compliance in the VEU program ): Essential Services Commission (VEU compliance and cold-call/doorknock reports): Phone (03) 9032 1310 or email veu@esc.vic.gov.au Consumer Affairs Victoria (contract, warranty, or consumer law disputes): Phone 131 450 Australian Do Not Call Register: Phone 1300 792 958 Frequently asked questions Are cold calls and doorknocking allowed under the Victorian Energy Upgrades program? No. Telemarketing cold calls have been banned since 1 May 2024 and doorknocking has been banned since 1 August 2024 under the VEU code of conduct, unless you have given express prior consent. Express prior consent given via an online enquiry form lasts for three months unless withdrawn sooner. Learn more about your rights on /how-quotes-work/. What must a VEU marketer or installer tell me, and what are they banned from saying? Under Essential Services Commission consumer rights rules, marketers must state that participating in VEU is voluntary and must never claim to work for the VEU program, the Essential Services Commission, or the Victorian Government, or tell you that an upgrade is mandatory when it is not. Where do I report a suspected VEU cold call, doorknock, or misleading offer? Contact the accredited provider first (providers must acknowledge complaints within five business days and aim to resolve them within 20 business days), or report non-compliance to the Essential Services Commission, Consumer Affairs Victoria, or the Australian Do Not Call Register using the official numbers listed on /victoria/veu-scams-cold-calls/. VEU offers market-based point-of-sale discounts through accredited providers to all Victorian households—including rentals—with no household income test or property value cap on its product pages. Solar Homes is administered by Solar Victoria for eligible owner-occupiers who meet income and property value caps, and rooftop solar PV support transitions into VEU from 1 July 2027. $150,000 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Solar Victoria ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Side-by-side comparison: VEU vs Solar Homes Feature Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) Solar Homes Program How it is funded Market-based VEEC certificates sold to energy retailers Victorian Government rebate administered by Solar Victoria How you claim Upfront point-of-sale discount via a VEU accredited provider Apply for Solar Victoria pre-approval before installation Household income cap No income test on VEU product pages ( Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling ) Under $150,000 [source] from 1 July 2026 (was $210,000 [source] until 30 June 2026) Property value cap No property value cap on VEU product pages Property valued under $3 million [source] Renters and rentals Eligible when tenant and landlord agree Hot water rebate is for owner-occupiers; separate rental solar PV settings exist Main household upgrades Reverse-cycle air con, heat pump & solar hot water, insulation, induction cooktops, draught proofing, glazing Hot water systems and rooftop solar panels (PV) Solar Homes 2026–27 caps and hot water stacking From 1 July 2026 , the combined household taxable income cap for Solar Homes fell to $150,000 [source] (down from $210,000 [source] ), alongside a property value limit under $3 million [source] , while the Victorian Government funded an extra 27,000 [source] hot water rebates for 2026–27 ( Solar Victoria — Targeted assistance update ; Solar Victoria — Hot water rebate ). Eligible owner-occupiers upgrading hot water can combine both programs on the same system—see how VEU and Solar Homes stack together and our Heat Pump Hot Water Rebate Victoria guide . Apartment owners and owners corporations can also compare shared options in our apartments and units guide . What happens to rooftop solar PV rebates in July 2027? Under current Solar Homes settings, eligible households can apply for a solar panel (PV) rebate of up to $1,400 [source] plus an optional matching interest-free loan ( Solar Victoria — Solar panel (PV) rebate ). Solar Victoria has announced that rooftop solar PV support will move into the Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program from 1 July 2027 , while existing Solar Homes solar PV rebate and loan arrangements stay in place until 30 June 2027 ( Solar Victoria — Solar support to continue through VEU ). Check your current heating, hot water, or home upgrade options in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Who runs Victorian Energy Upgrades versus the Solar Homes program? Victorian Energy Upgrades is regulated by the Essential Services Commission with policy set by Energy Victoria (DEECA) and delivered through accredited providers, whereas the Solar Homes program is administered directly by Solar Victoria with a formal pre-approval application. Does VEU have an income test like the Solar Homes program? No. Energy Victoria's household product pages state that all Victorian households are eligible for VEU discounts without a household income cap or property value cap, whereas Solar Homes hot water and solar panel rebates enforce both an income cap (reduced on 1 July 2026) and a property value cap. Check the exact caps on /victoria/veu-vs-solar-homes/. Can renters access both VEU discounts and Solar Homes hot water rebates? Private renters can access VEU discounts across heating, cooling, hot water, and other activities with their landlord's permission where required, whereas the standard Solar Homes hot water rebate is limited to owner-occupiers. Household Rebates Air Conditioner Rebate Heat Pump Rebate 2027 Gas Rule How Quotes Work Sources Check Eligibility Home Victoria What Is a VEEC and How Does It Fund Your VEU Discount? What Is a VEEC and How Does It Fund Your VEU Discount? A Victorian Energy Efficiency Certificate (VEEC) is a tradable certificate representing one tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent emissions saved when you install an approved energy upgrade. Accredited providers create VEECs from your upgrade and sell them to energy retailers, who are legally required to surrender certificates each year—and that certificate revenue funds your point-of-sale VEU discount. Because certificates trade on an open market rather than paying a fixed government cash grant, your final discount varies by product, location, provider, and market certificate value. $70 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · Energy Victoria (DEECA) ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 One certificate equals one tonne of emissions saved Under the Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) program, each Victorian Energy Efficiency Certificate (VEEC) represents one tonne of greenhouse gas emissions reduction ( CO2-e ) estimated over the lifetime of an approved energy-saving upgrade ( Essential Services Commission — Victorian Energy Efficiency Certificates (VEECs) ). Households do not create or trade VEECs themselves. Instead: You engage an accredited person (commonly called a VEU accredited provider) or a licensed installer working with one before your upgrade starts—see how VEU quotes and installers work . When you assign the right to create certificates to that accredited provider, they reduce your upfront invoice by an agreed point-of-sale discount ( Energy Victoria — About Victorian Energy Upgrades ). After installation and compliance checks, the accredited provider registers the VEECs with the Essential Services Commission and sells them to energy retailers , who must buy and surrender certificates each year to meet Victoria’s annual emissions targets. Why your VEU discount is not a fixed cash rebate Unlike a fixed-dollar government voucher—compare how VEU differs from the Solar Homes program —a VEU discount depends on four variables ( Energy Victoria — Insulation discounts ; Energy Victoria — Window glazing discounts ): Product efficiency and baseline: Replacing an inefficient electric resistance or gas appliance saves more lifetime emissions (and creates more VEECs) than replacing an already efficient unit—see the scenario tables on our Air Conditioner Rebate Victoria guide . Location: Metropolitan and regional Victoria have slightly different climate baselines in the VEU specifications. Provider administration costs: Accredited providers deduct compliance, auditing, and administration costs before passing the certificate value onto your quote, and you must always pay at least the mandatory VEU minimum co-payment . Certificate market value: Energy Victoria’s indicative product pages illustrate how certificate assumptions work—for example, Energy Victoria states that its indicative induction cooktop discount is based on $70 [source] per certificate ( Energy Victoria — Induction cooktop discounts ), which is the certificate price Energy Victoria based its induction figure on rather than a live market quote. We never publish trader certificate quotes because there is no official Victorian Government live price feed; your accredited provider confirms the exact dollar discount in your written quote. Upcoming rename to “energy upgrade certificates” (Act No. 37/2026) Under Victorian legislation passed in Act No. 37/2026 , the Victorian Energy Efficiency Target Act (VEET Act) will be renamed and VEECs will be renamed energy upgrade certificates on proclamation ( Essential Services Commission — VEU program legislation ). Until proclamation takes effect, official forms, quotes, and Essential Services Commission registers continue to refer to VEECs, and household eligibility works the same way—check your scenario in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions Who buys Victorian Energy Efficiency Certificates (VEECs)? Accredited persons create VEECs after an eligible energy upgrade is completed, and energy retailers buy and surrender those certificates each year to meet annual emissions targets enforced by the Essential Services Commission. Why does my VEU discount vary from one provider or postcode to another? Energy Victoria states that your final point-of-sale discount depends on current certificate market pricing, the specific product installed, your property's postcode location, and the accredited provider's administrative costs. Are VEECs being renamed under the 2026 legislation changes? Yes. Under Act No. 37/2026, on proclamation the Victorian Energy Efficiency Target Act will be renamed the Victorian Energy Upgrades Target Act and VEECs will be renamed energy upgrade certificates. Casey's municipal DIY rebate is claimed online with itemised product receipts and is completely separate from VEU provider-installed weather sealing, ceiling insulation, heating, and hot water discounts. up to $200 Checked on 13 Nov 2026 · City of Casey ↗ By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Local context for City of Casey (City of Casey) Postcodes covered on this page: 3805, 3806, 3976, 3977, 3978 The City of Casey offers a household rebate for eligible DIY draught-proofing products (one per household, receipts within 6 months, claimed online via Rebately). [City of Casey] Casey's municipal rebate cannot be claimed for paying a tradesperson, nor for ceiling insulation batts, double glazing, or heating system upgrades. [City of Casey] Residents can hire an Energy and Water Efficiency Home Audit Kit through the City of Casey to pinpoint air leaks and high-use appliances. What is excluded from the council rebate: You cannot claim Casey’s rebate for paying a tradesperson, nor for ceiling insulation batts, double glazing, or heating upgrades. Home Audit Kit: Residents can also hire an Energy and Water Efficiency Home Audit Kit from the council to find draughts around doors, skirting, and vents first. How Casey’s DIY rebate fits with VEU discounts Casey’s municipal DIY product rebate and Victorian Energy Upgrades (VEU) are separate programs: VEU weather sealing (provider-installed): When an accredited provider’s installer fits approved weather-sealing products across a detached house, Energy Victoria lists an indicative discount of $700 [source] for 5-year warranty products ( Energy Victoria — Weather sealing discounts ). Always read the mandatory carbon monoxide gas-heater safety rules first on our draught proofing (weather sealing) guide . Ceiling insulation and heating swaps: Because Casey postcodes ( 3805 , 3806 , 3976 , 3977 , 3978 ) sit in VEU’s Metropolitan / Mild classification like Melbourne ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ), compare metropolitan examples on our ceiling insulation guide and gas room heater to split system guide , or check your home in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . Frequently asked questions How does the City of Casey DIY draught-proofing rebate work? The City of Casey offers one household rebate for eligible DIY draught-proofing products purchased with receipts dated within six months, claimed online through the council’s Rebately portal while municipal funding remains open. Residents can also hire an Energy and Water Efficiency Home Audit Kit through the council. Can I use the City of Casey rebate to pay a tradesperson or buy ceiling insulation? No. City of Casey rules state that its DIY draught-proofing rebate cannot be claimed for paying a tradesperson, nor for ceiling insulation batts, double glazing, or heating system upgrades. How does Casey’s DIY rebate differ from VEU weather sealing? Casey’s council rebate reimburses eligible DIY draught-proofing materials you buy and fit yourself, whereas the Victorian Energy Upgrades weather sealing discount applies to approved products professionally installed through a VEU accredited provider. Remember to check for open-flued or flueless indoor gas appliances before sealing vents in any home. Impacted Solstice customers are exempt from Solar Victoria's standard household income cap, can replace a gas hot water system of any age, include rental providers, and can receive a dedicated top-up when VEU property or appliance age rules are not met. [Solar Victoria] Solar Victoria waives key standard rules for impacted Solstice customers: no household income cap applies, gas hot water units of any age can be replaced, rental providers can apply, and a dedicated top-up covers homes that miss VEU age rules. [Solar Victoria] Solar Victoria confirmed eight VEU accredited providers available across the ten impacted regional towns. Solstice Energy is closing its regional compressed natural gas (CNG) distribution networks by mid-to-late 2026 across ten Victorian towns : Marong , Heathcote , Swan Hill , Maldon , Robinvale , Kerang , Nathalia , Terang , Lakes Entrance , and Orbost ( Solar Victoria — Supporting Solstice Energy customers ). Note on the postcode table above: only Marong ( 3515 ) and Heathcote ( 3523 ) (within Greater Bendigo ) are listed in our verified postcode extract on this page; residents in the other eight towns should confirm their exact VEU postcode classification with one of the eight VEU accredited providers Solar Victoria confirmed as servicing the Solstice towns ( Solar Victoria — Supporting Solstice Energy customers ). Special Solar Victoria exemptions and top-up support To help impacted CNG customers move straight to electric appliances, Solar Victoria applies dedicated rule exemptions on top of standard VEU and Solar Homes stacking ( Solar Victoria — Supporting Solstice Energy customers ): No household income cap: Solar Homes’ usual combined taxable income cap ( $150,000 [source] ) does not apply to impacted Solstice CNG customers. Hot water system of any age: The standard three-year minimum age rule on existing hot water systems is waived for gas hot water to heat pump or solar hot water replacements. Rental providers eligible: Landlords of impacted Solstice properties can access support to electrify tenanted homes. Top-up when VEU rules are not met: Where a newer home (under two years old) or recently installed appliance does not qualify for a VEU discount, Solar Victoria provides a $600 [source] top-up ( Solar Victoria — Supporting Solstice Energy customers ). Going all-electric vs switching to bottled LPG Impacted households generally choose between converting gas appliances to bottled LPG or replacing them with reverse-cycle air conditioning, a heat pump water heater, and induction cooking. City of Greater Bendigo’s Marong study found that bottled LPG carries at least 2.5 times the running cost of running electric appliances ( City of Greater Bendigo — Support for Solstice Energy customers ). Map out your appliance order in the Get-Off-Gas Planner and check your property’s rebate pathways in the Victoria Rebate Eligibility Checker . What special Solar Victoria exemptions apply to impacted Solstice gas customers? Impacted Solstice Energy customers are exempt from the standard Solar Homes household income cap, can replace a gas hot water system of any age, include eligible rental providers, and can access a Solar Victoria top-up where a newer home or recent appliance does not meet standard VEU criteria. Solar Victoria also notes that eight VEU accredited providers confirmed availability across the ten towns. How do electric running costs compare with bottled LPG for Solstice towns? In a Marong household study published by the City of Greater Bendigo for Solstice-impacted customers, bottled LPG running costs were estimated at least 2.5 times higher than a partly or fully electric home. Read the council’s Solstice support page linked below for the full study assumptions. Council support includes borrowable library efficiency kits and interpreted webinars across six community languages, while homes built more than two years ago qualify for VEU heating and hot water replacement discounts through accredited providers. By Gurinder Singh, Agenor · Figures checked on 13 Nov 2026 against official Victorian sources · Updated 13 Nov 2026 Local context for Wyndham (Wyndham City Council) Postcodes covered on this page: 3024, 3029, 3030 Wyndham City runs the Energy Smart Homes program featuring recorded electrification workshops and a downloadable Your Go Electric Plan guide. Borrowable library kits: My Home Energy and Water Efficiency Kits can be borrowed from local Wyndham libraries to test standby power draw, draughts, and showerhead flow rates before spending money on upgrades. Before booking a quote in fast-growing estates across Tarneit, Truganina, Manor Lakes, or Point Cook, check your occupancy date: Homes more than 2 years old: Qualify for full VEU replacement discounts when swapping an old gas or electric unit ( Energy Victoria — Hot water system discounts ; Energy Victoria — Heating and cooling discounts ; see gas hot water to heat pump ). Frequently asked questions What does Wyndham City’s Energy Smart Homes program include? Wyndham City’s Energy Smart Homes program provides recorded electrification workshops, a downloadable Your Go Electric Plan resource, and links to Western Alliance for Greenhouse Action webinars. Residents can access these council resources alongside state-wide VEU and Solar Homes incentives. Can Wyndham residents borrow a home energy efficiency kit? Yes. Wyndham City makes My Home Energy and Water Efficiency Kits available to borrow through local Wyndham libraries so households can check appliance power draw, room temperatures, and water flow rates at home. Is energy help available in Punjabi and other community languages in Wyndham, and do new estates qualify for VEU? Through the Western Alliance for Greenhouse Action, interpreted Home Energy in Your Language webinars cover Arabic, Mandarin, Cantonese, Vietnamese, Sgaw Karen, and Punjabi for residents across six western councils including Wyndham. Note that in newer Werribee, Point Cook, and Tarneit estates, most VEU heating and hot water replacement discounts require your home to be more than two years old. Because Yarra Ranges spans outer-east valley suburbs, the Dandenong Ranges, and Upper Yarra towns, VEU Metropolitan/Regional, Mild/Cold, and heat pump zone 4/5 classifications vary by postcode rather than following a single shire-wide rule. No single VEU classification covers the entire shire ( VEU Specifications v25.0 PDF ): Metropolitan vs Regional: Most listed Yarra Ranges postcodes sit in Metropolitan , while Warburton ( 3799 ) sits in Regional . Mild vs Cold climatic region: Foothill postcodes such as 3139 and 3140 sit in Mild , whereas hills and valley postcodes ( 3770 , 3775 , 3777 , 3786 – 3788 , 3795 , 3796 ) sit in Cold —which affects certificate calculations for ceiling insulation upgrades and space heating. Heat pump zone 4 vs zone 5: Postcodes 3139 , 3140 , 3770 , 3775 , and 3777 sit in heat pump climatic zone 5 , while the remaining listed postcodes sit in zone 4 .
